## Purpose and Scope

This guide covers the complete training workflow for AESTETIK models, including model initialization, data preparation, loss computation, and training monitoring. It explains how to use the `fit()` method to train models on spatial transcriptomics data with both transcriptomics and morphology modalities.

For information about preparing data before training, see [Preparing Your Data](#4.1). For generating predictions with trained models, see [Making Predictions](#4.3). For complete API documentation, see [AESTETIK Class](#5.1).

---

## Training Workflow Overview

The training process in AESTETIK follows a structured pipeline orchestrated by PyTorch Lightning. The `AESTETIK.fit()` method coordinates all training steps, from data validation through model optimization.

### High-Level Training Sequence

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant fit as "AESTETIK.fit()"
    participant validate as "_validate_fit_inputs()"
    participant datamodule as "AESTETIKDataModule"
    participant model as "_build_model()"
    participant trainer as "Lightning Trainer"
    participant callbacks as "Callbacks"

    User->>fit: "fit(X, validation_split, ...)"
    fit->>validate: "validate inputs"
    validate-->>fit: "validation complete"
    fit->>datamodule: "initialize with parameters"
    datamodule-->>fit: "data prepared"
    fit->>model: "build AESTETIKModel"
    model-->>fit: "model ready"
    fit->>callbacks: "create callbacks"
    callbacks-->>fit: "callbacks configured"
    fit->>trainer: "fit(model, datamodule)"
    
    loop "Each Epoch"
        trainer->>model: "training_step(batch)"
        model-->>trainer: "loss"
        trainer->>callbacks: "on_train_epoch_end()"
    end
    
    trainer-->>fit: "training complete"
    fit-->>User: "self (fitted model)"
```

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:179-238]()

---

## The fit() Method

The `fit()` method is the primary entry point for training AESTETIK models. It handles the entire training pipeline from validation through optimization.

### Method Signature and Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `X` | `anndata.AnnData` | Required | AnnData object containing spatial transcriptomics data |
| `used_obsm_transcriptomics` | `str` | `"X_pca_transcriptomics"` | Key in `X.obsm` for transcriptomics features |
| `used_obsm_morphology` | `str` | `"X_pca_morphology"` | Key in `X.obsm` for morphology features |
| `used_obsm_combined` | `str` | `"X_pca"` | Key in `X.obsm` for combined features |
| `used_obs_batch` | `Optional[str]` | `None` | Key in `X.obs` for batch/sample labels |
| `validation_split` | `float` | `0.0` | Proportion of data to use for validation (0.0-1.0) |
| `early_stopping_params` | `Optional[dict]` | `None` | Parameters for early stopping callback |

### Required Data Structure

Before calling `fit()`, the AnnData object must contain:

| Location | Key | Content | Required |
|----------|-----|---------|----------|
| `X.obsm` | `used_obsm_transcriptomics` | Transcriptomics PCA features | Yes |
| `X.obsm` | `used_obsm_morphology` | Morphology PCA features | Yes |
| `X.obs` | `"x_array"` | Spatial x-coordinates | Yes |
| `X.obs` | `"y_array"` | Spatial y-coordinates | Yes |

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:179-209](), [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:337-343]()

---

## Training Initialization Process

The initialization phase prepares all components required for training, including parameter validation, batch size configuration, and model construction.

### Initialization Workflow

```mermaid
graph TB
    start["fit() called"]
    validate["_validate_fit_inputs()<br/>Check obsm keys & obs columns"]
    setparams["_set_fit_params()<br/>Set batch_size, obsm_transcriptomics_dim"]
    initdm["Initialize AESTETIKDataModule"]
    buildmodel["_build_model()<br/>Create AESTETIKModel"]
    createcb["_create_callbacks()<br/>Setup LossHistory, EarlyStopping, etc"]
    inittrainer["Initialize Lightning Trainer"]
    
    start-->validate
    validate-->setparams
    setparams-->initdm
    initdm-->buildmodel
    buildmodel-->createcb
    createcb-->inittrainer
    
    subgraph "Parameter Groups"
        grid["grid_params:<br/>morphology_dim, num_input_channels,<br/>obsm_transcriptomics_dim"]
        arch["model_architecture_params:<br/>latent_dim, c_hid, kernel_size,<br/>p, n_ensemble_encoder, n_ensemble_decoder"]
        train["training_params:<br/>lr, weight_decay, max_epochs"]
        loss["loss_regularization_params:<br/>rec_alpha, triplet_alpha,<br/>morphology_weight, transcriptomics_weight"]
    end
    
    setparams-.->grid
    buildmodel-.->arch
    buildmodel-.->train
    buildmodel-.->loss
```

### Automatic Batch Size Configuration

If `batch_size` is not specified during initialization, it is automatically set during the fit process:

```python
# From _set_fit_params()
if self.dataloader_params["batch_size"] is None:
    self.dataloader_params["batch_size"] = min(2 ** 13, len(X))
```

This ensures the batch size is at most 8192 or the dataset size, whichever is smaller.

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:210-227](), [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:398-404](), [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:525-541]()

---

## Model Architecture Construction

The `_build_model()` method constructs the `AESTETIKModel` Lightning module, which wraps the core autoencoder architecture.

### Model Building Components

```mermaid
graph LR
    buildmodel["_build_model()"]
    trainparams["training_step_params<br/>{rec_alpha, triplet_alpha}"]
    optimparams["optimizer_step_params<br/>{lr, weight_decay}"]
    litmodel["AESTETIKModel"]
    
    subgraph "Input Parameters"
        datamodule["datamodule:<br/>AESTETIKDataModule"]
        gridparams["grid_params"]
        archparams["model_architecture_params"]
    end
    
    buildmodel-->trainparams
    buildmodel-->optimparams
    datamodule-->litmodel
    gridparams-->litmodel
    archparams-->litmodel
    trainparams-->litmodel
    optimparams-->litmodel
    
    subgraph "AESTETIKModel Setup"
        configmodel["configure_model()<br/>Build AE autoencoder"]
        setup["setup()<br/>Initialize weights & loss functions"]
        configopt["configure_optimizers()<br/>Create Adam optimizer"]
    end
    
    litmodel-.->configmodel
    litmodel-.->setup
    litmodel-.->configopt
```

### Model Configuration Process

The `AESTETIKModel.configure_model()` method is called automatically by Lightning to build the actual autoencoder:

| Step | Action | Code Location |
|------|--------|---------------|
| 1. Get grid dimensions | Extract from `X.obsm["X_st_grid"]` | [src/aestetik/modules/aestetik_module.py:84-86]() |
| 2. Update grid_params | Set `morphology_dim` and `num_input_channels` | [src/aestetik/modules/aestetik_module.py:85-86]() |
| 3. Build AE model | Initialize ensemble encoder/decoder | [src/aestetik/modules/aestetik_module.py:88-89]() |
| 4. Set model_built flag | Prevent re-initialization | [src/aestetik/modules/aestetik_module.py:90]() |

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:525-541](), [src/aestetik/modules/aestetik_module.py:80-91](), [src/aestetik/modules/aestetik_module.py:14-55]()

---

## Training Loop Execution

Once initialized, the Lightning `Trainer` manages the training loop, calling `training_step()` for each batch.

### Training Step Data Flow

```mermaid
graph TB
    batch["Batch from DataLoader"]
    unpack["Unpack batch:<br/>anchor, pos_trans, neg_trans,<br/>pos_morph, neg_morph"]
    forward["model(anchor)<br/>Returns: anchor_encode, anchor_decode"]
    compute["compute_loss()<br/>Calculate all loss components"]
    
    batch-->unpack
    unpack-->forward
    forward-->compute
    
    subgraph "Loss Components"
        rectrans["rec_loss_transcriptomics<br/>(L1Loss)"]
        recmorph["rec_loss_morphology<br/>(L1Loss)"]
        triptrans["triplet_loss_transcriptomics<br/>(TripletMarginLoss)"]
        tripmorph["triplet_loss_morphology<br/>(TripletMarginLoss)"]
        total["total_loss<br/>(weighted sum)"]
    end
    
    compute-->rectrans
    compute-->recmorph
    compute-->triptrans
    compute-->tripmorph
    rectrans-->total
    recmorph-->total
    triptrans-->total
    tripmorph-->total
    
    subgraph "Logging"
        logl["log('L', total_loss)"]
        logrc["log('RC', rec_loss_trans)"]
        logri["log('RI', rec_loss_morph)"]
        logtc["log('TC', triplet_loss_trans)"]
        logti["log('TI', triplet_loss_morph)"]
    end
    
    total-->logl
    rectrans-->logrc
    recmorph-->logri
    triptrans-->logtc
    tripmorph-->logti
```

### training_step() Implementation

The `training_step()` method in `AESTETIKModel` performs the following operations:

1. **Unpack batch**: Extract anchor, positive samples, and negative samples for both modalities
2. **Forward pass**: Run anchor through the encoder and decoder
3. **Compute loss**: Calculate reconstruction and triplet losses for both modalities
4. **Log metrics**: Record all loss components for monitoring
5. **Return total loss**: Used for backpropagation

```python
# Batch structure: (anchor, pos_trans_list, neg_trans_list, pos_morph_list, neg_morph_list)
# Each list contains multiple samples for multi-triplet loss computation
```

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/modules/aestetik_module.py:93-117](), [example/gettingStartedWithAESTETIK.ipynb:318-320]()

---

## Loss Computation Details

AESTETIK uses a multi-component loss function that combines reconstruction and contrastive learning objectives for both modalities.

### Loss Function Components

| Loss Type | Purpose | Weight Parameter | Loss Function |
|-----------|---------|------------------|---------------|
| Reconstruction (Transcriptomics) | Reconstruct transcriptomics features | `rec_alpha` × `transcriptomics_weight` | L1Loss |
| Reconstruction (Morphology) | Reconstruct morphology features | `rec_alpha` × `morphology_weight` | L1Loss |
| Triplet (Transcriptomics) | Separate transcriptomics clusters | `triplet_alpha` × `transcriptomics_weight` | TripletMarginLoss |
| Triplet (Morphology) | Separate morphology clusters | `triplet_alpha` × `morphology_weight` | TripletMarginLoss |

### Loss Weighting Formula

```
total_loss = (rec_alpha × transcriptomics_weight × rec_loss_trans) +
             (rec_alpha × morphology_weight × rec_loss_morph) +
             (triplet_alpha × transcriptomics_weight × triplet_loss_trans) +
             (triplet_alpha × morphology_weight × triplet_loss_morph)
```

### Loss Function Initialization

Loss functions are initialized in the `setup()` method:

```python
self.loss = {
    "triplet_loss": nn.TripletMarginLoss(),
    "rec_loss": nn.L1Loss()
}
```

The modality weights are calibrated automatically during data preparation based on clustering quality, then normalized to sum to `total_weight` (default: 3).

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/modules/aestetik_module.py:74-77](), [src/aestetik/modules/aestetik_module.py:99-111](), [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:153-161]()

---

## Monitoring and Callbacks

AESTETIK provides several mechanisms for monitoring training progress and implementing training controls.

### Callback System Architecture

```mermaid
graph TB
    trainer["Lightning Trainer"]
    losscb["LossHistoryCallback<br/>(Always active)"]
    earlystop["EarlyStopping<br/>(If validation_split > 0)"]
    checkpoint["ModelCheckpoint<br/>(If validation_split > 0)"]
    
    trainer-->losscb
    trainer-->earlystop
    trainer-->checkpoint
    
    subgraph "LossHistoryCallback"
        onepoch["on_train_epoch_end()"]
        store["Store: L, RC, RI, TC, TI"]
        losses["model.losses dict"]
    end
    
    losscb-.->onepoch
    onepoch-->store
    store-->losses
    
    subgraph "EarlyStopping Config"
        monitor["monitor: 'val_loss'"]
        mode["mode: 'min'"]
        patience["patience: 5 (default)"]
    end
    
    earlystop-.->monitor
    earlystop-.->mode
    earlystop-.->patience
    
    subgraph "ModelCheckpoint Config"
        monitorck["monitor: 'val_loss'"]
        modeck["mode: 'min'"]
        topk["save_top_k: 1"]
        filename["filename: 'best-checkpoint'"]
    end
    
    checkpoint-.->monitorck
    checkpoint-.->modeck
    checkpoint-.->topk
    checkpoint-.->filename
```

### Accessing Training Losses

After training, loss history is available through the model:

```python
model.fit(X=adata)
losses = model.losses  # Dictionary with keys: 'L', 'RC', 'RI', 'TC', 'TI'
```

### Loss Metric Keys

| Key | Full Name | Description |
|-----|-----------|-------------|
| `L` | Total Loss | Weighted sum of all loss components |
| `RC` | Reconstruction (Transcriptomics) | L1 loss for transcriptomics reconstruction |
| `RI` | Reconstruction (Morphology) | L1 loss for morphology reconstruction |
| `TC` | Triplet (Transcriptomics) | Triplet margin loss for transcriptomics |
| `TI` | Triplet (Morphology) | Triplet margin loss for morphology |

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:231-238](), [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:449-467](), [src/aestetik/modules/aestetik_module.py:112-116]()

---

## Validation and Early Stopping

When `validation_split > 0.0`, AESTETIK automatically enables validation monitoring and optional early stopping.

### Validation Configuration

```mermaid
graph LR
    fit["fit(validation_split=0.2)"]
    datamodule["AESTETIKDataModule<br/>Creates train/val split"]
    callbacks["_create_callbacks()"]
    
    fit-->datamodule
    fit-->callbacks
    
    subgraph "Validation Setup"
        split["Split data:<br/>80% train, 20% validation"]
        valloader["Create validation DataLoader"]
    end
    
    datamodule-.->split
    split-->valloader
    
    subgraph "Callback Creation"
        earlystop["EarlyStopping"]
        checkpoint["ModelCheckpoint"]
        params["early_stopping_params"]
    end
    
    callbacks-->earlystop
    callbacks-->checkpoint
    params-.->earlystop
    
    subgraph "Early Stopping Defaults"
        monitordef["monitor: 'val_loss'"]
        modedef["mode: 'min'"]
        patiencedef["patience: 5"]
    end
    
    earlystop-.->monitordef
    earlystop-.->modedef
    earlystop-.->patiencedef
```

### Configuring Early Stopping

The `early_stopping_params` dictionary accepts the following keys:

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `patience` | `int` | `5` | Number of epochs with no improvement before stopping |
| `min_delta` | `float` | `0.0` | Minimum change in monitored metric to qualify as improvement |

**Note:** The `monitor` and `mode` parameters are fixed to `"val_loss"` and `"min"` respectively and cannot be overridden.

### validation_step() Behavior

The validation step differs from training in one key aspect: dropout is still active (model in training mode) but gradients are disabled:

```python
def validation_step(self, batch, batch_idx):
    self.model.train()  # Keep dropout active for stochastic validation
    with torch.no_grad():  # Disable gradient computation
        # Compute losses without backpropagation
```

This provides validation estimates that account for model stochasticity.

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:203-208](), [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:449-484](), [src/aestetik/modules/aestetik_module.py:119-140]()

---

## Trainer Configuration

The Lightning `Trainer` is configured with specific parameters optimized for AESTETIK's training regime.

### Trainer Initialization Parameters

```python
self.trainer = Trainer(
    max_epochs=self.training_params["max_epochs"],
    callbacks=callbacks,
    num_sanity_val_steps=0
)
```

| Parameter | Value | Explanation |
|-----------|-------|-------------|
| `max_epochs` | From `training_params` | Maximum training epochs (default: 100) |
| `callbacks` | List | LossHistoryCallback + optional EarlyStopping/ModelCheckpoint |
| `num_sanity_val_steps` | `0` | Disables sanity validation checks to avoid unnecessary computation |

### Training Execution Flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant fit as "AESTETIK.fit()"
    participant Trainer
    participant Model as "AESTETIKModel"
    participant DataModule
    
    fit->>Trainer: "Trainer.fit(model, datamodule)"
    
    loop "For each epoch"
        Trainer->>DataModule: "train_dataloader()"
        DataModule-->>Trainer: "batches"
        
        loop "For each batch"
            Trainer->>Model: "training_step(batch, batch_idx)"
            Model->>Model: "forward pass"
            Model->>Model: "compute_loss()"
            Model-->>Trainer: "total_loss"
            Trainer->>Trainer: "backward() & optimizer.step()"
        end
        
        alt "validation_split > 0"
            Trainer->>DataModule: "val_dataloader()"
            DataModule-->>Trainer: "val_batches"
            
            loop "For each val batch"
                Trainer->>Model: "validation_step(batch, batch_idx)"
                Model-->>Trainer: "val_loss"
            end
            
            Trainer->>Trainer: "Check early stopping"
        end
        
        Trainer->>Trainer: "callbacks.on_epoch_end()"
    end
    
    Trainer-->>fit: "training complete"
```

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:234-237]()

---

## Optimizer Configuration

AESTETIK uses the Adam optimizer with AMSGrad variant for stable training.

### Optimizer Setup

```python
def configure_optimizers(self):
    optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(
        self.model.parameters(),
        amsgrad=True,
        lr=self.hparams["optimizer_params"]["lr"],
        weight_decay=self.hparams["optimizer_params"]["weight_decay"]
    )
    return optimizer
```

### Optimizer Parameters

| Parameter | Default Value | Description |
|-----------|---------------|-------------|
| `lr` | `0.001` | Learning rate for gradient descent |
| `weight_decay` | `1e-6` | L2 regularization coefficient |
| `amsgrad` | `True` | Use AMSGrad variant for more stable convergence |

The AMSGrad variant maintains the maximum of squared gradients, which can help with convergence in non-convex optimization problems.

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/modules/aestetik_module.py:163-168](), [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:84-85](), [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:109]()

---

## Practical Training Examples

### Basic Training Example

```python
from aestetik import AESTETIK
import scanpy as sc

# Load and prepare data
adata = sc.read_h5ad("data.h5ad")

# Initialize model
model = AESTETIK(
    nCluster=7,
    morphology_weight=0.5,
    max_epochs=50
)

# Train model
model.fit(X=adata)

# Access training losses
losses = model.losses
print(f"Final total loss: {losses['L'][-1]}")
```

### Training with Validation and Early Stopping

```python
# Train with validation split
model.fit(
    X=adata,
    validation_split=0.2,
    early_stopping_params={
        'patience': 10,
        'min_delta': 0.001
    }
)
```

### Training with Custom Modality Keys

```python
# Use custom keys for multi-sample data
model.fit(
    X=adata,
    used_obsm_transcriptomics="custom_trans_pca",
    used_obsm_morphology="custom_morph_pca",
    used_obs_batch="sample_id"  # For batch-aware processing
)
```

### Monitoring Training Progress

```python
from aestetik.utils.utils_visualization import visualize

# Train model
model.fit(X=adata, validation_split=0.15)

# Visualize training loss curves
visualize(model=model, plot_loss=True)
```

**Sources:** [example/gettingStartedWithAESTETIK.ipynb:289-320](), [example/gettingStartedWithAESTETIK.ipynb:396-398]()

## Common Training Parameters

### Model Architecture Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Range | Impact |
|-----------|---------|-------|--------|
| `window_size` | `7` | Odd integers ≥ 3 | Size of spatial neighborhood grid |
| `latent_dim` | `16` | 8-64 typical | Dimensionality of learned representations |
| `c_hid` | `64` | 32-128 typical | Hidden channel dimension in CNN |
| `kernel_size` | `3` | 1 to window_size-1 | Convolution kernel size |
| `p` | `0.3` | 0.0-0.5 | Dropout probability for regularization |
| `n_ensemble` | `3` | 1-10 | Number of ensemble encoders/decoders |

### Loss Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Range | Impact |
|-----------|---------|-------|--------|
| `morphology_weight` | Required | 0.0-3.0 | Weight for morphology modality |
| `rec_alpha` | `1.0` | 0.1-10.0 | Scaling factor for reconstruction loss |
| `triplet_alpha` | `1.0` | 0.1-10.0 | Scaling factor for triplet loss |
| `total_weight` | `3.0` | 1.0-5.0 | Total weight (transcriptomics + morphology) |

### Training Control Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Range | Impact |
|-----------|---------|-------|--------|
| `max_epochs` | `100` | 10-1000 | Maximum training epochs |
| `lr` | `0.001` | 1e-5 to 1e-2 | Learning rate |
| `batch_size` | Auto | 32-8192 | Batch size (auto: min(8192, n_spots)) |
| `weight_decay` | `1e-6` | 1e-8 to 1e-4 | L2 regularization strength |

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:29-116](), [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:126-166]()

---

## Training Output and Artifacts

### Model State After Training

After `fit()` completes, the `AESTETIK` object contains:

| Attribute | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `lit_aestetik_model` | `AESTETIKModel` | Trained Lightning module |
| `trainer` | `Trainer` | Lightning Trainer instance |
| `losses` | `dict` | Loss history for each metric |

### Using the Trained Model

```python
# Check if model is fitted
if model.trainer is not None:
    print("Model is trained and ready for prediction")

# Access loss history
for metric, values in model.losses.items():
    print(f"{metric}: {len(values)} epochs recorded")

# Generate predictions
model.predict(X=adata, cluster=True)
```

### Training State Validation

The `_check_fitted()` method ensures the model is trained before prediction:

```python
def _check_fitted(self):
    if self.trainer is None or self.lit_aestetik_model is None:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "The model has not been fitted yet. Call 'fit' before 'predict'."
        )
```

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:170-171](), [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:369-371](), [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:238]()

# Page: Making Predictions

# Making Predictions

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md)
- [example/gettingStartedWithAESTETIK.ipynb](example/gettingStartedWithAESTETIK.ipynb)
- [example/gettingStartedWithAESTETIKwithSimulatedData.ipynb](example/gettingStartedWithAESTETIKwithSimulatedData.ipynb)
- [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py](src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This page describes how to generate latent space embeddings from a trained AESTETIK model and optionally perform clustering on those embeddings. It covers the `predict()` and `fit_predict()` methods, cross-sample prediction capabilities, input validation, and output formatting.

For information about training models, see [Training Models](#4.2). For information about analyzing and visualizing the predicted embeddings and clusters, see [Clustering and Analysis](#4.4) and [Visualization](#4.5). For detailed API specifications, see [AESTETIK Class](#5.1).

---

## Overview

AESTETIK provides two methods for generating predictions:

| Method | Use Case | When to Use |
|--------|----------|-------------|
| `predict()` | Generate embeddings from a trained model | Cross-sample prediction, applying pre-trained model to new data |
| `fit_predict()` | Train and immediately predict | Single-sample workflow, convenience method |

Both methods:
- Compute latent space representations via stochastic forward passes (Monte Carlo dropout)
- Store embeddings in `adata.obsm`
- Optionally perform clustering and store results in `adata.obs`
- Support multi-sample datasets via batch labels

Sources: [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:240-332]()

---

## Prediction Methods

### The predict() Method

The `predict()` method generates embeddings from an already-fitted model. This is the primary method for cross-sample prediction.

```mermaid
graph TB
    Input["predict(X, num_repeats, cluster, ...)"]
    Check["_check_fitted()"]
    Validate["_validate_predict_inputs()"]
    Calibrate["_calibrate_predict_inputs()"]
    SetParams["_set_predict_params()"]
    Compute["_compute_latent_space()"]
    PostProcess["_postprocess_predictions()"]
    Output["Embeddings stored in X.obsm"]
    
    Input --> Check
    Check --> Validate
    Validate --> Calibrate
    Calibrate --> SetParams
    SetParams --> Compute
    Compute --> PostProcess
    PostProcess --> Output
    
    Check -.->|"raises RuntimeError"| Error["Model not fitted"]
    Validate -.->|"raises KeyError/ValueError"| Error2["Invalid inputs"]
```

**Method signature:**
```python
def predict(
    X: anndata.AnnData,
    used_obsm_transcriptomics: str = "X_pca_transcriptomics",
    used_obsm_morphology: str = "X_pca_morphology",
    used_obs_batch: Optional[str] = None,
    save_emb: str = "AESTETIK",
    num_repeats: int = 1000,
    cluster: bool = True
) -> None
```

**Key parameters:**
- `X`: AnnData object containing the data to predict on (can be different from training data)
- `num_repeats`: Number of stochastic forward passes (Monte Carlo dropout) to average
- `cluster`: Whether to perform clustering after computing embeddings
- `save_emb`: Key for storing embeddings in `X.obsm`

Sources: [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:240-282]()

### The fit_predict() Method

The `fit_predict()` method combines training and prediction in a single call. It is a convenience method for single-sample workflows.

```python
def fit_predict(
    X: anndata.AnnData,
    used_obsm_transcriptomics: str = "X_pca_transcriptomics",
    used_obsm_morphology: str = "X_pca_morphology",
    used_obsm_combined: str = "X_pca",
    used_obs_batch: Optional[str] = None,
    validation_split: float = 0.0,
    save_emb: str = "AESTETIK",
    num_repeats: int = 1000,
    cluster: bool = True
) -> None
```

**Implementation detail:** This method internally calls `fit()` followed by `_compute_latent_space()` with `built_grid=True` to avoid rebuilding the spatial grid.

Sources: [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:284-332]()

---

## Prediction Workflow

### High-Level Prediction Pipeline

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Input Validation"
        A["Check Model Fitted"]
        B["Validate obsm Keys"]
        C["Validate obs Columns"]
        D["Check Dimensionality"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Input Calibration"
        E["Calibrate Transcriptomics Dims"]
        F["Calibrate Morphology Dims"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Latent Space Computation"
        G["Build Spatial Grid"]
        H["Create DataLoader"]
        I["Stochastic Forward Passes"]
        J["Average Embeddings"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Post-Processing"
        K["Store in obsm"]
        L["Optional Clustering"]
        M["Store in obs"]
    end
    
    A --> B
    B --> C
    C --> D
    D --> E
    E --> F
    F --> G
    G --> H
    H --> I
    I --> J
    J --> K
    K --> L
    L --> M
```

Sources: [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:240-282](), [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:489-520]()

### Input Validation and Calibration

The prediction workflow begins with strict validation to ensure compatibility between the input data and the trained model.

**Validation checks:**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Start["predict() called"]
    Check1{"Model fitted?"}
    Check2{"Required obsm keys present?"}
    Check3{"x_array, y_array in obs?"}
    Check4{"Dimensionality compatible?"}
    Calibrate["_calibrate_predict_inputs()"]
    Proceed["Continue to prediction"]
    
    Start --> Check1
    Check1 -->|"No"| Error1["RuntimeError"]
    Check1 -->|"Yes"| Check2
    Check2 -->|"No"| Error2["KeyError"]
    Check2 -->|"Yes"| Check3
    Check3 -->|"No"| Error3["KeyError"]
    Check3 -->|"Yes"| Check4
    Check4 -->|"Too small"| Error4["ValueError"]
    Check4 -->|"OK or larger"| Calibrate
    Calibrate --> Proceed
```

**Validation methods:**
- `_check_fitted()`: Ensures `self.trainer` and `self.lit_aestetik_model` are not None
- `_validate_predict_inputs()`: Checks for required keys and dimensionality
- `_calibrate_predict_inputs()`: Truncates oversized features to match training dimensions

**Calibration example:**
```python
# If prediction data has more features than training data used
# Transcriptomics: trained with 15 dims, prediction has 20 dims
# System automatically truncates to 15 dims
X.obsm[used_obsm_transcriptomics] = X.obsm[used_obsm_transcriptomics][:, :15]
```

Sources: [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:369-425]()

### Latent Space Computation

The core prediction operation uses **Monte Carlo dropout** to generate robust embeddings by averaging multiple stochastic forward passes.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Predict as "_compute_latent_space()"
    participant DataLoader as "_create_predict_dataloader()"
    participant Grid as "build_grid()"
    participant Trainer as "Lightning Trainer"
    participant Model as "AESTETIKModel"
    participant Encoder as "AE Encoder Ensemble"
    
    Predict->>DataLoader: Create prediction dataloader
    alt built_grid=False
        DataLoader->>Grid: build_grid(X, ...)
        Grid-->>DataLoader: X.obsm["X_st_grid"]
    end
    DataLoader->>DataLoader: Create TensorDataset
    DataLoader-->>Predict: DataLoader instance
    
    Predict->>Trainer: predict(model, dataloader)
    
    loop Each batch
        loop num_repeats times
            Trainer->>Model: predict_step(batch)
            Model->>Encoder: forward(batch)
            Note over Model,Encoder: Dropout enabled<br/>Stochastic output
            Encoder-->>Model: latent_space_i
            Model-->>Trainer: latent_space_i
        end
        Trainer->>Trainer: Average num_repeats outputs
    end
    
    Trainer-->>Predict: all_latent_space (concatenated)
```

**Key implementation details:**

| Component | File Location | Role |
|-----------|---------------|------|
| `_compute_latent_space()` | [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:489-503]() | Orchestrates latent space computation |
| `_create_predict_dataloader()` | [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:428-447]() | Builds DataLoader from spatial grids |
| `build_grid()` | [src/aestetik/utils/utils_data.py]() | Constructs spatial grids if not cached |
| `AESTETIKModel.predict_step()` | [src/aestetik/modules/aestetik_module.py]() | Performs stochastic forward pass |

**num_repeats parameter:**
- Default: 1000 forward passes per batch
- Higher values: More stable embeddings but slower computation
- Set via `_set_predict_params()` which updates `self.lit_aestetik_model.predict_params["num_repeats"]`

Sources: [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:406-447](), [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:489-503]()

### Post-Processing

After computing latent space embeddings, the `_postprocess_predictions()` method stores results and optionally performs clustering.

```mermaid
graph TB
    Input["latent_space (torch.Tensor)"]
    Convert["Convert to numpy"]
    Store["X.obsm[save_emb] = embeddings"]
    CheckCluster{"cluster=True?"}
    Clustering["clustering()"]
    StoreCluster["Store in X.obs"]
    Done["Complete"]
    
    Input --> Convert
    Convert --> Store
    Store --> CheckCluster
    CheckCluster -->|"Yes"| Clustering
    CheckCluster -->|"No"| Done
    Clustering --> StoreCluster
    StoreCluster --> Done
```

**Output locations:**

| Data | Storage Location | Key Name | Format |
|------|------------------|----------|--------|
| Embeddings | `X.obsm` | `save_emb` (default: "AESTETIK") | numpy array (n_spots, latent_dim) |
| Cluster labels | `X.obs` | `{save_emb}_cluster` | categorical |
| Refined clusters | `X.obs` | `{save_emb}_cluster_refined` | categorical |

**Clustering invocation:**
```python
if cluster:
    clustering(
        X,
        used_obsm=save_emb,
        num_cluster=self.clustering_params["nCluster"],
        method=self.clustering_params["clustering_method"],
        refine_cluster=self.clustering_params["refine_cluster"],
        n_neighbors=self.clustering_params["n_neighbors"],
        used_obs_batch=used_obs_batch
    )
```

Sources: [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:505-520]()

---

## Cross-Sample Prediction

A key capability of AESTETIK is **cross-sample prediction**: training on one spatial transcriptomics sample and applying the model to different samples.

### When to Use Cross-Sample Prediction

| Scenario | Approach |
|----------|----------|
| Training and prediction on same sample | Use `fit_predict()` |
| Applying model to new samples | Use `fit()` then `predict()` |
| Batch correction across samples | Use `used_obs_batch` parameter |
| Transfer learning | Train on annotated sample, predict on unlabeled samples |

### Cross-Sample Prediction Workflow

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Training Phase"
        Train1["Sample A: adata_train"]
        Train2["model = AESTETIK(...)"]
        Train3["model.fit(adata_train)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Prediction Phase"
        Pred1["Sample B: adata_test"]
        Pred2["Validate compatibility"]
        Pred3["model.predict(adata_test)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Compatibility Requirements"
        Req1["Same feature keys in obsm"]
        Req2["Feature dims >= training dims"]
        Req3["Spatial coordinates in obs"]
    end
    
    Train1 --> Train2
    Train2 --> Train3
    Train3 -.->|"Trained model"| Pred2
    Pred1 --> Pred2
    Pred2 --> Pred3
    
    Req1 -.-> Pred2
    Req2 -.-> Pred2
    Req3 -.-> Pred2
```

### Compatibility Requirements

For cross-sample prediction to work, the test data must meet specific requirements:

**Required AnnData structure:**

| Component | Requirement | Validation Method |
|-----------|-------------|-------------------|
| `obsm` keys | `used_obsm_transcriptomics` and `used_obsm_morphology` must exist | `_validate_obsm_keys()` |
| `obs` columns | `x_array` and `y_array` must exist | `_validate_obs_columns()` |
| Feature dimensions | Must be ≥ training dimensions | `_validate_predict_inputs()` |

**Automatic calibration:**
- If test data has more features than training data, features are automatically truncated
- Transcriptomics truncated to `grid_params["obsm_transcriptomics_dim"]`
- Morphology truncated to `grid_params["num_input_channels"] - grid_params["obsm_transcriptomics_dim"]`

### Multi-Sample Datasets

AESTETIK supports predictions on multi-sample datasets using batch labels:

```python
# adata contains multiple samples with batch column
model.predict(
    X=adata,
    used_obs_batch="sample_id",  # Column identifying samples
    cluster=True
)
```

When `used_obs_batch` is provided:
- Spatial grids are built separately per sample
- Clustering can account for batch effects
- Results are stored for all samples simultaneously

Sources: [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:345-425](), [CHANGELOG.md:36-38]()

---

## Parameters

### Core Prediction Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `X` | `anndata.AnnData` | Required | Input data with features in `obsm` and coordinates in `obs` |
| `num_repeats` | `int` | 1000 | Number of stochastic forward passes for Monte Carlo dropout |
| `cluster` | `bool` | True | Whether to perform clustering after computing embeddings |
| `save_emb` | `str` | "AESTETIK" | Key for storing embeddings in `X.obsm` |

### Feature Keys

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `used_obsm_transcriptomics` | `str` | "X_pca_transcriptomics" | Key for transcriptomics features in `X.obsm` |
| `used_obsm_morphology` | `str` | "X_pca_morphology" | Key for morphology features in `X.obsm` |
| `used_obs_batch` | `Optional[str]` | None | Column name in `X.obs` for sample identifiers |

### Additional Parameters (fit_predict only)

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `used_obsm_combined` | `str` | "X_pca" | Key for combined features (used during training) |
| `validation_split` | `float` | 0.0 | Proportion of data for validation during training |

Sources: [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:240-332]()

---

## Output Format

### Embeddings in obsm

Embeddings are stored as numpy arrays in `X.obsm[save_emb]`:

```python
# After prediction
embeddings = adata.obsm["AESTETIK"]  # Shape: (n_spots, latent_dim)

# latent_dim is specified during model initialization (default: 16)
# Each row corresponds to one spot's latent representation
```

### Clustering Results in obs

If `cluster=True`, clustering results are stored in `X.obs`:

| Column Name | Format | Description |
|-------------|--------|-------------|
| `{save_emb}_cluster` | categorical | Initial cluster assignments |
| `{save_emb}_cluster_refined` | categorical | Spatially refined clusters (if `refine_cluster=True`) |

**Additional metadata columns:**

For multi-modal clustering, the system also stores intermediate clustering results:
- `X_pca_transcriptomics_cluster`: Clusters from transcriptomics modality only
- `X_pca_morphology_cluster`: Clusters from morphology modality only

Sources: [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:505-520](), [example/gettingStartedWithAESTETIK.ipynb:363]()

---

## Examples

### Example 1: Basic Prediction

```python
# After training (see Training Models page)
model = AESTETIK(nCluster=7, morphology_weight=1.5)
model.fit(X=adata_train)

# Generate embeddings and cluster
model.predict(X=adata_train, cluster=True)

# Access results
embeddings = adata_train.obsm["AESTETIK"]
clusters = adata_train.obs["AESTETIK_cluster"]
```

Sources: [example/gettingStartedWithAESTETIK.ipynb:341]()

### Example 2: Cross-Sample Prediction

```python
# Train on sample A
model = AESTETIK(nCluster=5, morphology_weight=1.0)
model.fit(X=adata_sample_a)

# Predict on sample B (different tissue section)
# Must have same feature keys and >= dimensions
model.predict(
    X=adata_sample_b,
    num_repeats=2000,  # More repeats for stability
    cluster=True
)

# Results stored in adata_sample_b
embeddings_b = adata_sample_b.obsm["AESTETIK"]
```

Sources: [CHANGELOG.md:36-38]()

### Example 3: Multi-Sample Dataset

```python
# Dataset with multiple samples identified by 'sample_id' column
model = AESTETIK(nCluster=6, morphology_weight=1.2)
model.fit(X=adata_multi, used_obs_batch="sample_id")

# Predict on the same or different multi-sample dataset
model.predict(
    X=adata_multi,
    used_obs_batch="sample_id",
    save_emb="AESTETIK_multi",
    cluster=True
)
```

Sources: [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:244](), [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:262]()

### Example 4: Custom Feature Keys

```python
# Use custom keys for features
model.predict(
    X=adata,
    used_obsm_transcriptomics="my_transcriptomics_pca",
    used_obsm_morphology="my_morphology_features",
    save_emb="custom_embeddings",
    cluster=False  # Skip clustering, just get embeddings
)

# Access embeddings
embeddings = adata.obsm["custom_embeddings"]
```

### Example 5: fit_predict Convenience Method

```python
# Train and predict in one call
model = AESTETIK(nCluster=5, morphology_weight=0)
model.fit_predict(
    X=adata,
    num_repeats=1500,
    cluster=True
)

# Results immediately available
clusters = adata.obs["AESTETIK_cluster"]
```

Sources: [example/gettingStartedWithAESTETIKwithSimulatedData.ipynb:244]()

---

## Technical Details

### Spatial Grid Construction During Prediction

When `built_grid=False` (cross-sample prediction), the system must construct spatial grids:

```mermaid
graph LR
    A["X.obsm features"]
    B["X.obs coordinates"]
    C["build_grid()"]
    D["X.obsm['X_st_grid']"]
    E["TensorDataset"]
    F["DataLoader"]
    
    A --> C
    B --> C
    C --> D
    D --> E
    E --> F
```

**Grid construction parameters:**
- `window_size`: Taken from `grid_params["morphology_dim"]` (set during initialization)
- `n_jobs`: Parallelization level from `data_handling_params["n_jobs"]`

Sources: [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:428-447]()

### DataLoader Configuration

Prediction uses the same DataLoader configuration as training:

| Parameter | Source | Description |
|-----------|--------|-------------|
| `batch_size` | `dataloader_params["batch_size"]` | Batch size for prediction |
| `num_workers` | `dataloader_params["num_workers"]` | Parallel data loading workers |
| `shuffle` | False (fixed) | No shuffling during prediction |

Sources: [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:445-447]()

### Stochastic Forward Passes Implementation

The actual stochastic forward passes are implemented in the `AESTETIKModel.predict_step()` method:

```mermaid
graph TB
    Input["Batch from DataLoader"]
    Loop["Repeat num_repeats times"]
    Forward["encoder(batch) with dropout"]
    Collect["Collect latent vectors"]
    Average["Mean over repeats"]
    Output["Averaged latent space"]
    
    Input --> Loop
    Loop --> Forward
    Forward --> Collect
    Collect --> Average
    Average --> Output
```

The averaging provides robustness against dropout randomness and produces more stable embeddings.

Sources: [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:406-408](), [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:500-503]()

---

## Common Issues and Solutions

| Issue | Cause | Solution |
|-------|-------|----------|
| `RuntimeError: Model not fitted` | Calling `predict()` before `fit()` | Call `fit()` first or use `fit_predict()` |
| `KeyError: Required keys missing` | Missing feature keys in test data | Ensure same keys used for training exist in test data |
| `ValueError: Dimensionality too small` | Test data has fewer features than training | Provide data with at least as many features as training |
| Memory error with large datasets | Too many `num_repeats` or large `batch_size` | Reduce `num_repeats` or `batch_size` |
| Predictions differ from training sample | Natural variation with Monte Carlo dropout | Increase `num_repeats` for more stable results |

Sources: [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:369-425]()

---

# Page: Clustering and Analysis

# Clustering and Analysis

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [example/gettingStartedWithAESTETIK.ipynb](example/gettingStartedWithAESTETIK.ipynb)
- [example/gettingStartedWithAESTETIKwithSimulatedData.ipynb](example/gettingStartedWithAESTETIKwithSimulatedData.ipynb)
- [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py](src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py)
- [src/aestetik/utils/utils_clustering.py](src/aestetik/utils/utils_clustering.py)

</details>



This page provides a practical guide to clustering embeddings generated by AESTETIK and analyzing the resulting spatial domains. It covers the automatic clustering features integrated into the prediction workflow, manual clustering approaches, available clustering methods, spatial refinement techniques, and methods for determining optimal cluster numbers.

For information about generating embeddings before clustering, see [Making Predictions](#4.3). For visualizing clustering results, see [Visualization](#4.5). For detailed API reference of clustering utilities, see [Utility Functions](#5.4).

## Overview of Clustering Workflow

AESTETIK provides two primary approaches for clustering spatial transcriptomics data:

1. **Automatic Clustering**: Integrated into the `predict()` or `fit_predict()` methods
2. **Manual Clustering**: Using standalone utility functions for custom workflows

```mermaid
graph TB
    Embeddings["Latent Space Embeddings<br/>adata.obsm['AESTETIK']"]
    
    AutoCluster["Automatic Clustering<br/>model.predict(cluster=True)"]
    ManualCluster["Manual Clustering<br/>utils_clustering.clustering()"]
    
    Method["Clustering Method Selection<br/>bgm | kmeans | leiden | louvain"]
    
    InitialClusters["Initial Cluster Assignments<br/>adata.obs['AESTETIK_cluster']"]
    
    Refine["Spatial Refinement<br/>_refine_cluster()"]
    
    FinalClusters["Refined Cluster Assignments<br/>adata.obs['AESTETIK_cluster']"]
    
    Analysis["Downstream Analysis<br/>squidpy | scanpy"]
    
    Embeddings --> AutoCluster
    Embeddings --> ManualCluster
    
    AutoCluster --> Method
    ManualCluster --> Method
    
    Method --> InitialClusters
    
    InitialClusters --> Refine
    Refine --> FinalClusters
    
    InitialClusters -.->|"refine_cluster=False"| Analysis
    FinalClusters --> Analysis
```

Sources: [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:240-283](), [src/aestetik/utils/utils_clustering.py:140-211]()

## Automatic Clustering During Prediction

The simplest way to perform clustering is through the `cluster` parameter in the `predict()` method. This automatically clusters the latent space embeddings after they are computed.

### Basic Usage

```python
# Compute embeddings and cluster in one step
model.predict(X=adata, cluster=True)

# Access results
embeddings = adata.obsm["AESTETIK"]           # Latent space embeddings
clusters = adata.obs["AESTETIK_cluster"]      # Cluster assignments
```

### Parameter Flow

| Parameter | Initialization Location | Effect |
|-----------|------------------------|---------|
| `nCluster` | `AESTETIK.__init__()` | Number of clusters or resolution parameter |
| `clustering_method` | `AESTETIK.__init__()` | Algorithm: "bgm", "kmeans", "leiden", "louvain" |
| `refine_cluster` | `AESTETIK.__init__()` | Whether to apply spatial refinement |
| `n_neighbors` | `AESTETIK.__init__()` | Number of neighbors for spatial refinement |
| `cluster` | `predict()` method | Whether to perform clustering at all |

The clustering is triggered by the `_postprocess_predictions()` method:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant AESTETIK
    participant PostProcess as "_postprocess_predictions"
    participant Clustering as "utils_clustering.clustering"
    participant Refine as "_refine_cluster"
    
    User->>AESTETIK: predict(adata, cluster=True)
    AESTETIK->>AESTETIK: _compute_latent_space()
    AESTETIK->>PostProcess: _postprocess_predictions()
    
    PostProcess->>PostProcess: "Store embeddings in adata.obsm"
    
    alt cluster=True
        PostProcess->>Clustering: "clustering(adata, used_obsm='AESTETIK')"
        Clustering->>Clustering: "Apply selected method"
        
        alt refine_cluster=True
            Clustering->>Refine: "_refine_cluster()"
            Refine->>Refine: "KNN spatial refinement"
            Refine-->>Clustering: "Refined clusters"
        end
        
        Clustering-->>PostProcess: "Store in adata.obs"
    end
    
    PostProcess-->>AESTETIK: "adata modified in-place"
    AESTETIK-->>User: "None"
```

Sources: [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:505-521](), [src/aestetik/utils/utils_clustering.py:140-211]()

## Clustering Methods

AESTETIK supports four clustering algorithms, each suited for different analysis scenarios.

### Method Comparison

| Method | Type | `nCluster` Parameter | Best For | Output Probability |
|--------|------|---------------------|----------|-------------------|
| **bgm** | Bayesian Gaussian Mixture | Integer (number of components) | Uncertainty quantification, soft clustering | Yes |
| **kmeans** | K-Means | Integer (number of clusters) | Fast, well-separated clusters | No |
| **leiden** | Community Detection | Float (resolution) or Integer (target clusters) | Graph-based, biological relevance | No |
| **louvain** | Community Detection | Float (resolution) or Integer (target clusters) | Graph-based, modularity optimization | No |

### Bayesian Gaussian Mixture (BGM)

The default method using `BayesianGaussianMixture` from scikit-learn. Provides probabilistic cluster assignments and is robust to cluster shape variations.

**Implementation Details:**
- Uses tied covariance matrices across components
- 1000 max iterations with 10 random initializations
- Stores cluster probabilities in `adata.obs[f"{used_obsm}_cluster_proba"]`

**Configuration:**
```python
model = AESTETIK(
    nCluster=7,                    # Number of mixture components
    clustering_method="bgm",
    refine_cluster=True
)
```

Sources: [src/aestetik/utils/utils_clustering.py:188-201]()

### K-Means

Fast and deterministic clustering using `KMeans` with 100 initializations for stability.

**Configuration:**
```python
model = AESTETIK(
    nCluster=5,                    # Number of clusters
    clustering_method="kmeans",
    refine_cluster=True
)
```

Sources: [src/aestetik/utils/utils_clustering.py:183-187]()

### Leiden and Louvain

Graph-based community detection methods from scanpy. These methods build a k-nearest neighbor graph (k=50) and optimize for community structure.

**Resolution-Based Clustering:**
```python
# Use resolution parameter directly
model = AESTETIK(
    nCluster=1.0,                  # Resolution parameter (float)
    clustering_method="leiden"
)
```

**Target Cluster Count:**
```python
# Automatically search for resolution that yields target count
model = AESTETIK(
    nCluster=7,                    # Desired number of clusters (int)
    clustering_method="leiden"
)
# Uses search_res() to find appropriate resolution
```

The `search_res()` function performs binary search to find the resolution parameter that produces the desired number of clusters:

Sources: [src/aestetik/utils/utils_clustering.py:83-137](), [src/aestetik/utils/utils_clustering.py:154-182]()

## Spatial Cluster Refinement

Spatial refinement uses the physical coordinates of spots to improve clustering coherence. This is particularly important for spatial transcriptomics where neighboring spots are more likely to belong to the same biological domain.

### Refinement Algorithm

```mermaid
graph TB
    InitClusters["Initial Cluster Assignments"]
    
    CheckProba{"Probability<br/>Available?"}
    
    HighConf["High Confidence Spots<br/>proba > conf_proba"]
    AllSpots["All Spots"]
    
    BuildKNN["Build KNN Classifier<br/>KNeighborsClassifier(n_neighbors)"]
    
    SpatialCoords["Spatial Coordinates<br/>x_array, y_array"]
    
    Predict["Predict All Spots<br/>Based on Spatial Neighbors"]
    
    RefinedClusters["Refined Cluster Assignments"]
    
    InitClusters --> CheckProba
    
    CheckProba -->|"Yes (BGM)"| HighConf
    CheckProba -->|"No"| AllSpots
    
    HighConf --> BuildKNN
    AllSpots --> BuildKNN
    
    SpatialCoords --> BuildKNN
    
    BuildKNN --> Predict
    Predict --> RefinedClusters
```

### Key Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Description |
|-----------|---------|-------------|
| `refine_cluster` | `True` | Enable spatial refinement |
| `n_neighbors` | 10 | Number of spatial neighbors to consider |
| `conf_proba` | 0.9 | Minimum probability threshold for training set (BGM only) |

### Implementation Details

The refinement process is handled by `_refine_cluster()` which:

1. **Probability-Based Training** (BGM only): Uses only high-confidence spots (probability > 0.9) to train the KNN classifier
2. **Spatial Feature Space**: Uses `x_array` and `y_array` coordinates as features
3. **KNN Prediction**: Classifies all spots based on majority vote of spatial neighbors
4. **Batch-Aware**: Applies refinement separately within each batch if `used_obs_batch` is specified

**Example with Refinement:**
```python
# Enable spatial refinement with custom parameters
model = AESTETIK(
    nCluster=7,
    clustering_method="bgm",
    refine_cluster=True,
    n_neighbors=15              # Use 15 spatial neighbors
)

model.fit_predict(adata)
```

Sources: [src/aestetik/utils/utils_clustering.py:203-275]()

## Determining Optimal Cluster Numbers

AESTETIK provides utilities to help determine the appropriate number of clusters for your data.

### Using find_optimal_n_clusters()

This function evaluates clustering quality across a range of cluster numbers using two metrics:

1. **Silhouette Score**: Measures cluster separation quality (higher is better)
2. **Sum of Squared Errors (SSE)**: Measures within-cluster variance (lower is better)

Both metrics are computed separately for transcriptomics and morphology modalities.

**Usage:**
```python
from aestetik.utils.utils_clustering import find_optimal_n_clusters

# Test cluster numbers from 2 to 10
find_optimal_n_clusters(
    adata, 
    start=2, 
    end=10, 
    suggested_n=7  # Optional reference line
)
```

**Output:**
- Two-panel plot showing silhouette scores and SSE across cluster numbers
- Separate lines for transcriptomics and morphology modalities
- Normalized SSE values for easier comparison
- Optional vertical line at `suggested_n` for reference

```mermaid
graph LR
    Data["Input AnnData<br/>X_pca_transcriptomics<br/>X_pca_morphology"]
    
    Loop["Iterate k=start to end"]
    
    KMeans_T["KMeans on<br/>Transcriptomics"]
    KMeans_M["KMeans on<br/>Morphology"]
    
    Metrics_T["Compute SSE & Silhouette<br/>for Transcriptomics"]
    Metrics_M["Compute SSE & Silhouette<br/>for Morphology"]
    
    Plot["Generate Comparison Plot<br/>plotnine visualization"]
    
    Data --> Loop
    Loop --> KMeans_T
    Loop --> KMeans_M
    
    KMeans_T --> Metrics_T
    KMeans_M --> Metrics_M
    
    Metrics_T --> Plot
    Metrics_M --> Plot
```

**Interpretation Guidelines:**
- **Silhouette Score Peak**: Indicates well-separated clusters
- **SSE Elbow**: Point where SSE decrease slows significantly
- **Modality Agreement**: Look for cluster numbers where both modalities show good metrics
- **Biological Relevance**: Consider known tissue structure when choosing final number

Sources: [src/aestetik/utils/utils_clustering.py:18-80]()

## Working with Clustering Results

After clustering, results are stored in the AnnData object following scanpy conventions.

### Output Structure

| Location | Key | Content |
|----------|-----|---------|
| `adata.obsm` | `"AESTETIK"` | Latent space embeddings (n_spots × latent_dim) |
| `adata.obs` | `"AESTETIK_cluster"` | Cluster assignments as strings |
| `adata.obs` | `"AESTETIK_cluster_proba"` | Cluster probabilities (BGM only) |

### Example Analysis Workflow

```python
# 1. Perform clustering
model = AESTETIK(nCluster=7, clustering_method="bgm", refine_cluster=True)
model.fit_predict(adata)

# 2. Access results
embeddings = adata.obsm["AESTETIK"]
clusters = adata.obs["AESTETIK_cluster"]
probabilities = adata.obs["AESTETIK_cluster_proba"]  # If using BGM

# 3. Compute UMAP on embeddings
import scanpy as sc
sc.pp.neighbors(adata, use_rep="AESTETIK")
sc.tl.umap(adata)

# 4. Visualize in embedding space
sc.pl.umap(adata, color=["AESTETIK_cluster", "ground_truth"])

# 5. Visualize in spatial context
import squidpy as sq
sq.pl.spatial_scatter(adata, color="AESTETIK_cluster")

# 6. Identify uncertain spots (BGM only)
uncertain_spots = adata[adata.obs["AESTETIK_cluster_proba"] < 0.8]
```

Sources: [example/gettingStartedWithAESTETIK.ipynb:329-398](), [example/gettingStartedWithAESTETIKwithSimulatedData.ipynb:244-296]()

## Batch-Aware Clustering

When working with multi-sample datasets, AESTETIK can perform batch-aware clustering that respects sample boundaries during spatial refinement.

### Configuration

```python
# Train on multi-sample dataset
model = AESTETIK(
    nCluster=7,
    clustering_method="bgm",
    refine_cluster=True,
    n_neighbors=10
)

# Specify batch column during prediction
model.predict(
    adata,
    cluster=True,
    used_obs_batch="sample_id"  # Column in adata.obs with sample labels
)
```

### Batch-Aware Refinement Process

```mermaid
graph TB
    Clusters["Initial Cluster Assignments<br/>All Samples Combined"]
    
    CheckBatch{"used_obs_batch<br/>specified?"}
    
    GlobalRefine["Global Refinement<br/>_refine() on all data"]
    
    BatchLoop["For each batch_id"]
    
    ExtractBatch["Extract batch subset<br/>mask = adata.obs[used_obs_batch] == batch_id"]
    
    BatchRefine["Batch Refinement<br/>_refine() on subset"]
    
    UpdateGlobal["Update global adata.obs"]
    
    FinalClusters["Final Cluster Assignments"]
    
    Clusters --> CheckBatch
    
    CheckBatch -->|"No"| GlobalRefine
    CheckBatch -->|"Yes"| BatchLoop
    
    GlobalRefine --> FinalClusters
    
    BatchLoop --> ExtractBatch
    ExtractBatch --> BatchRefine
    BatchRefine --> UpdateGlobal
    UpdateGlobal --> BatchLoop
    
    BatchLoop --> FinalClusters
```

**Key Benefits:**
1. **Independent Spatial Refinement**: Each sample's spatial structure is respected
2. **Prevents Cross-Sample Contamination**: Spatial neighbors only considered within same sample
3. **Consistent Cluster Labels**: Cluster identities maintained across samples

**Implementation:**
- The `_refine_cluster()` function checks for `used_obs_batch` parameter
- When provided, loops through unique batch values
- Applies `_refine()` independently to each batch subset
- Updates cluster assignments back to original AnnData object

Sources: [src/aestetik/utils/utils_clustering.py:212-247](), [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:505-521]()

## Manual Clustering Workflow

For advanced users who need more control, the clustering functions can be called directly.

### Direct Function Call

```python
from aestetik.utils.utils_clustering import clustering

# Cluster pre-computed embeddings
clustering(
    adata,
    used_obsm="AESTETIK",          # Key in adata.obsm
    num_cluster=7,
    method="bgm",
    refine_cluster=True,
    n_neighbors=10,
    used_obs_batch=None
)

# Results stored in adata.obs["AESTETIK_cluster"]
```

### Custom Clustering Parameters

```python
# Example: Higher confidence threshold for BGM refinement
clustering(
    adata,
    used_obsm="custom_embedding",
    num_cluster=5,
    method="bgm",
    refine_cluster=True,
    n_neighbors=15,
    conf_proba=0.95,               # More stringent confidence
    used_obs_batch="sample_id"
)
```

### Resolution Search Parameters

For leiden/louvain methods with target cluster counts:

```python
# Custom resolution search range
clustering(
    adata,
    used_obsm="AESTETIK",
    num_cluster=8,                 # Target cluster count
    method="leiden",
    refine_cluster=True,
    start=0.1,                     # Minimum resolution to try
    end=5.0,                       # Maximum resolution to try
    increment=0.05                 # Step size
)
```

Sources: [src/aestetik/utils/utils_clustering.py:140-211]()

## Integration with Downstream Analysis

AESTETIK clustering results integrate seamlessly with scanpy and squidpy workflows.

### Spatial Statistics

```python
import squidpy as sq

# Compute spatial autocorrelation of clusters
sq.gr.spatial_autocorr(
    adata,
    mode="moran",
    genes=adata.obs["AESTETIK_cluster"].unique()
)

# Compute neighborhood enrichment
sq.gr.nhood_enrichment(adata, cluster_key="AESTETIK_cluster")

# Compute co-occurrence scores
sq.gr.co_occurrence(
    adata,
    cluster_key="AESTETIK_cluster"
)
```

### Differential Expression by Cluster

```python
import scanpy as sc

# Find marker genes for each cluster
sc.tl.rank_genes_groups(
    adata,
    groupby="AESTETIK_cluster",
    method="wilcoxon"
)

# Plot top markers
sc.pl.rank_genes_groups(adata, n_genes=10)
```

### Cluster Quality Assessment

```python
from sklearn.metrics import silhouette_score, adjusted_rand_score

# Silhouette score on embeddings
silhouette = silhouette_score(
    adata.obsm["AESTETIK"],
    adata.obs["AESTETIK_cluster"]
)

# Compare to ground truth (if available)
if "ground_truth" in adata.obs:
    ari = adjusted_rand_score(
        adata.obs["ground_truth"],
        adata.obs["AESTETIK_cluster"]
    )
```

Sources: [example/gettingStartedWithAESTETIK.ipynb:363-398](), [example/gettingStartedWithAESTETIKwithSimulatedData.ipynb:254-296]()

# Page: Visualization

# Visualization

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

## Purpose and Scope

This page covers visualization capabilities in AESTETIK for analyzing model training, spatial clusters, embeddings, and representative spots. For information about the underlying model architecture, see [Model Architecture](#5.3). For details on clustering algorithms, see [Clustering and Analysis](#4.4).

## Overview

AESTETIK provides visualization tools through two primary mechanisms:

1. **Native visualization function**: [`visualize()`](src/aestetik/utils/utils_visualization.py:30-102) in `utils_visualization.py`
2. **Ecosystem integration**: Direct compatibility with `scanpy` and `squidpy` plotting functions

The `visualize()` function serves as a unified interface for common visualization tasks, while the ecosystem integration allows users to leverage the full power of established spatial transcriptomics visualization libraries.

**Sources**: [src/aestetik/utils/utils_visualization.py:1-256](), [example/gettingStartedWithAESTETIK.ipynb:396-397]()

## Visualization Workflow

```mermaid
graph TB

    VizFunc -->|"reads"| AnnData

```

## Training Progress Visualization

### Loss Plots

The `visualize()` function tracks and visualizes training loss across iterations using the model's stored loss history. This helps assess convergence and diagnose training issues.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `model` | `AESTETIK` | Fitted AESTETIK model containing loss history |
| `plot_loss` | `bool` | Set to `True` to display loss plot |

**Usage Example**:
```python
from aestetik.utils.utils_visualization import visualize

visualize(model=model, plot_loss=True)
```

The function accesses [`model.losses`](src/aestetik/utils/utils_visualization.py:81) and generates a line plot showing loss values over training iterations using [`_plot_loss_values()`](src/aestetik/utils/utils_visualization.py:107-111).

**Sources**: [src/aestetik/utils/utils_visualization.py:80-81](), [src/aestetik/utils/utils_visualization.py:107-111](), [example/gettingStartedWithAESTETIK.ipynb:396-397]()

## Spatial Cluster Visualization

### Cluster Comparison with ARI

The cluster visualization functionality compares spatial clustering results across different modalities and computes Adjusted Rand Index (ARI) scores against ground truth labels when available.

```mermaid
graph LR
    Input["adata.obs"]
    
    subgraph "Cluster Sources"
        TransCluster["X_pca_transcriptomics_cluster"]
        MorphCluster["X_pca_morphology_cluster"]
        AestCluster["AESTETIK_cluster"]
        GroundTruth["ground_truth"]
    end
    
    subgraph "ARI Computation"
        ARICalc["adjusted_rand_score()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Visualization"
        SpatialScatter["sq.pl.spatial_scatter()"]
        Titles["Labels with ARI"]
    end
    
    Input --> TransCluster
    Input --> MorphCluster
    Input --> AestCluster
    Input --> GroundTruth
    
    TransCluster --> ARICalc
    MorphCluster --> ARICalc
    AestCluster --> ARICalc
    GroundTruth --> ARICalc
    
    ARICalc --> Titles
    Titles --> SpatialScatter
    TransCluster --> SpatialScatter
    MorphCluster --> SpatialScatter
    AestCluster --> SpatialScatter
```

The [`_plot_spatial_scatter_ari()`](src/aestetik/utils/utils_visualization.py:129-161) function:
1. Collects cluster labels from specified obsm keys
2. Computes ARI scores using [`adjusted_rand_score()`](src/aestetik/utils/utils_visualization.py:145-147)
3. Generates spatial scatter plots via [`sq.pl.spatial_scatter()`](src/aestetik/utils/utils_visualization.py:155-161)

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `adata` | `anndata.AnnData` | Required | AnnData object with cluster labels |
| `plot_clusters` | `bool` | `False` | Enable cluster visualization |
| `used_obsm_transcriptomics` | `str` | `"X_pca_transcriptomics"` | Key for transcriptomics data |
| `used_obsm_morphology` | `str` | `"X_pca_morphology"` | Key for morphology data |
| `img_alpha` | `float` | `0.6` | Image opacity (0-1) |
| `dot_size` | `int` | `5` | Size of spatial spots |
| `ncols` | `int` | `5` | Number of columns in plot grid |

**Sources**: [src/aestetik/utils/utils_visualization.py:82-89](), [src/aestetik/utils/utils_visualization.py:129-161]()

## Centroid Analysis and Visualization

### Centroid Computation

AESTETIK identifies representative spots (centroids) for each cluster in the learned embedding space using scikit-learn's [`NearestCentroid`](src/aestetik/utils/utils_visualization.py:202) classifier.

```mermaid
graph TB
    Embedding["adata.obsm[save_emb]"]
    Labels["adata.obs[save_emb + '_cluster']"]
    
    subgraph "Centroid Detection"
        NC["NearestCentroid"]
        NCFit["nc.fit()"]
        Centroids["nc.centroids_"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Distance Computation"
        CDist["cdist()"]
        DistMatrix["Distance Matrix<br/>n_clusters × n_spots"]
        TopN["np.argpartition()<br/>Select top N closest"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Storage"
        CentroidCol["adata.obs['centroid']"]
        DistCols["adata.obs['dist_from_X']"]
    end
    
    Embedding --> NC
    Labels --> NC
    NC --> NCFit
    NCFit --> Centroids
    
    Centroids --> CDist
    Embedding --> CDist
    CDist --> DistMatrix
    DistMatrix --> TopN
    
    TopN --> CentroidCol
    DistMatrix --> DistCols
```

The [`_compute_centroid()`](src/aestetik/utils/utils_visualization.py:198-217) function:

1. Fits a [`NearestCentroid`](src/aestetik/utils/utils_visualization.py:202) classifier on embeddings
2. Computes distances from all spots to each centroid using [`cdist()`](src/aestetik/utils/utils_visualization.py:205)
3. Identifies top N closest spots per cluster using [`np.argpartition()`](src/aestetik/utils/utils_visualization.py:209)
4. Stores centroid labels in [`adata.obs["centroid"]`](src/aestetik/utils/utils_visualization.py:207)
5. Stores normalized distances in columns like `dist_from_0`, `dist_from_1`, etc. [(lines 214-216)](src/aestetik/utils/utils_visualization.py:214-216)

**Sources**: [src/aestetik/utils/utils_visualization.py:198-217]()

### Spatial Centroid Visualization

The [`_plot_spatial_centroids_and_distance()`](src/aestetik/utils/utils_visualization.py:114-126) function visualizes:
- Cluster assignments
- Identified centroids
- Distance gradients from each cluster centroid

This uses [`sq.pl.spatial_scatter()`](src/aestetik/utils/utils_visualization.py:120-126) to display the cluster column, centroid column, and all distance columns in a multi-panel plot.

**Sources**: [src/aestetik/utils/utils_visualization.py:114-126]()

### Morphology Spot Extraction

For centroids, AESTETIK can extract and display the corresponding H&E image patches using PyVips for efficient large image handling.

```mermaid
graph TB
    ImgPath["img_path"]
    SpotCoords["adata.obs[['x_pixel', 'y_pixel']]"]
    Diameter["spot_diameter_fullres"]
    CentroidIdx["topN_centroid_idx"]
    
    subgraph "Image Processing"
        PyVips["pyvips.Image.new_from_file()"]
        GetSpot["_get_spot()"]
        Crop["image.crop()"]
        ToArray["write_to_memory()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Visualization"
        PlotSpots["_plot_spots()"]
        MatplotlibGrid["Matplotlib Grid<br/>rows × columns"]
    end
    
    ImgPath --> PyVips
    PyVips --> GetSpot
    SpotCoords --> GetSpot
    Diameter --> GetSpot
    GetSpot --> Crop
    Crop --> ToArray
    
    CentroidIdx --> PlotSpots
    ToArray --> PlotSpots
    PlotSpots --> MatplotlibGrid
```

The image extraction pipeline [(lines 186-193)](src/aestetik/utils/utils_visualization.py:186-193):
1. Opens the full-resolution image using [`pyvips.Image.new_from_file()`](src/aestetik/utils/utils_visualization.py:165)
2. Crops a square region centered on each spot using [`image.crop()`](src/aestetik/utils/utils_visualization.py:189)
3. Converts to numpy array via [`write_to_memory()`](src/aestetik/utils/utils_visualization.py:190-192)

The [`_plot_spots()`](src/aestetik/utils/utils_visualization.py:163-181) function arranges extracted spots in a grid, showing up to 10 columns per row.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `img_path` | `str` | Path to full-resolution H&E image |
| `spot_diameter_fullres` | `int` | Spot diameter in pixels at full resolution |
| `plot_centroid` | `bool` | Enable centroid visualization |
| `topN` | `int` | Number of representative spots per cluster (default: 5) |

**Sources**: [src/aestetik/utils/utils_visualization.py:163-193](), [src/aestetik/utils/utils_visualization.py:219-233]()

## Integration with Scanpy/Squidpy

AESTETIK embeddings and cluster assignments are stored following scanpy conventions, enabling direct use with ecosystem visualization tools.

### Storage Conventions

| AnnData Location | Content | Key |
|------------------|---------|-----|
| `adata.obsm["AESTETIK"]` | Latent embeddings | User-configurable via `save_emb` parameter |
| `adata.obs["AESTETIK_cluster"]` | Cluster assignments | `{save_emb}_cluster` |
| `adata.obs["X_pca_transcriptomics_cluster"]` | Pre-training transcriptomics clusters | From data preparation |
| `adata.obs["X_pca_morphology_cluster"]` | Pre-training morphology clusters | From data preparation |

### Scanpy Visualization Examples

```python
# UMAP visualization
sc.pp.neighbors(adata, use_rep="AESTETIK")
sc.tl.umap(adata)
sc.pl.umap(adata, color=["ground_truth", "AESTETIK_cluster"])
```

The notebooks demonstrate this pattern at [example/gettingStartedWithAESTETIKwithSimulatedData.ipynb:254-259]().

### Squidpy Spatial Visualization

```python
# Spatial scatter plots
sq.pl.spatial_scatter(
    adata, 
    color=["ground_truth", 
           "X_pca_transcriptomics_cluster",
           "X_pca_morphology_cluster",
           "AESTETIK_cluster"], 
    size=dot_size
)
```

Example usage at [example/gettingStartedWithAESTETIK.ipynb:375-378]() and [example/gettingStartedWithAESTETIKwithSimulatedData.ipynb:269-275]().

**Sources**: [example/gettingStartedWithAESTETIK.ipynb:375-378](), [example/gettingStartedWithAESTETIKwithSimulatedData.ipynb:254-275]()

## Parameter Reference

### Core `visualize()` Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required When | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|---------------|-------------|
| `model` | `AESTETIK` | - | Always | Fitted AESTETIK model instance |
| `adata` | `anndata.AnnData` | `None` | `plot_clusters=True` or `plot_centroid=True` | AnnData object with results |
| `img_path` | `str` | `None` | `plot_centroid=True` | Path to H&E image for morphology extraction |
| `spot_diameter_fullres` | `int` | `None` | `plot_centroid=True` | Spot diameter in pixels |
| `save_emb` | `str` | `"AESTETIK"` | - | Key prefix for embeddings and clusters in AnnData |
| `plot_loss` | `bool` | `False` | - | Display training loss plot |
| `plot_clusters` | `bool` | `False` | - | Display spatial cluster comparison |
| `plot_centroid` | `bool` | `False` | - | Display centroids and morphology |

### Display Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `img_alpha` | `float` | `0.6` | Opacity for background H&E image (0.0-1.0) |
| `dot_size` | `int` | `5` | Size of spots in spatial scatter plots |
| `ncols` | `int` | `5` | Number of columns in multi-panel plots |
| `used_obsm_transcriptomics` | `str` | `"X_pca_transcriptomics"` | obsm key for transcriptomics features |
| `used_obsm_morphology` | `str` | `"X_pca_morphology"` | obsm key for morphology features |

**Sources**: [src/aestetik/utils/utils_visualization.py:30-72]()

## Input Validation

The [`_validate_visualize_inputs()`](src/aestetik/utils/utils_visualization.py:238-255) function enforces requirements:

- `adata` must be provided when `plot_clusters=True` or `plot_centroid=True`
- Multiple clusters required when `plot_centroid=True` [(line 253-254)](src/aestetik/utils/utils_visualization.py:253-254)
- `img_path` and `spot_diameter_fullres` required when `plot_centroid=True` [(line 255)](src/aestetik/utils/utils_visualization.py:255)

Error messages clearly indicate missing dependencies and suggest corrective actions.

**Sources**: [src/aestetik/utils/utils_visualization.py:238-255]()

## Complete Usage Example

```python
from aestetik import AESTETIK
from aestetik.utils.utils_visualization import visualize

# After training and prediction
model = AESTETIK(nCluster=7)
model.fit(adata)
model.predict(adata, cluster=True)

# Comprehensive visualization
visualize(
    model=model,
    adata=adata,
    img_path="path/to/image.png",
    spot_diameter_fullres=180,
    plot_loss=True,           # Training convergence
    plot_clusters=True,       # Spatial comparison with ARI
    plot_centroid=True,       # Representative spots
    img_alpha=0.6,
    dot_size=5,
    ncols=5
)
```

This produces:
1. Training loss curve over iterations
2. Spatial scatter plots comparing all clustering approaches with ARI scores
3. Centroid locations and distance gradients  
4. H&E image patches for top representative spots per cluster

**Sources**: [example/gettingStartedWithAESTETIK.ipynb:396-397](), [src/aestetik/utils/utils_visualization.py:30-102]()

# Page: API Reference

# API Reference

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md)
- [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py](src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py)

</details>



This section provides comprehensive reference documentation for all public APIs and classes in AESTETIK. The API is organized into four major components: the main orchestrator class, data pipeline components, model architecture classes, and utility functions.

**Scope**: This page covers the high-level organization of the AESTETIK API and common usage patterns. For detailed documentation on specific classes and functions, see the respective subsections:
- For the main `AESTETIK` class and its methods (`fit()`, `predict()`, `fit_predict()`), see [AESTETIK Class](#5.1)
- For data loading and preprocessing components, see [Data Pipeline Components](#5.2)
- For neural network architecture and Lightning integration, see [Model Architecture](#5.3)
- For clustering, visualization, and other utilities, see [Utility Functions](#5.4)

For conceptual explanations of how these components work together, see [Core Concepts](#3). For practical usage examples, see [User Guide](#4).

---

## API Organization

The AESTETIK API is structured in layers, with the `AESTETIK` class serving as the main public interface that orchestrates underlying components.

### Component Hierarchy

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Public API Layer"
        AESTETIK["AESTETIK class<br/>(src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Data Processing Layer"
        DataModule["AESTETIKDataModule<br/>(src/aestetik/data_modules/data_module.py)"]
        UtilsData["prepare_input_for_model()<br/>(src/aestetik/utils/utils_data.py)"]
        UtilsGrid["build_grid()<br/>(src/aestetik/utils/utils_grid.py)"]
        UtilsClustering["clustering()<br/>(src/aestetik/utils/utils_clustering.py)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Model Layer"
        LitModel["AESTETIKModel<br/>(src/aestetik/modules/aestetik_module.py)"]
        AE["AE class<br/>(src/aestetik/models/ae.py)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Analysis Layer"
        UtilsViz["visualize()<br/>(src/aestetik/utils/utils_visualization.py)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "External Interfaces"
        AnnData["anndata.AnnData"]
        Trainer["lightning.Trainer"]
    end
    
    AESTETIK -->|"initializes"| DataModule
    AESTETIK -->|"builds"| LitModel
    AESTETIK -->|"uses"| Trainer
    AESTETIK -->|"reads/writes"| AnnData
    
    DataModule -->|"calls"| UtilsData
    DataModule -->|"calls"| UtilsGrid
    UtilsData -->|"calls"| UtilsClustering
    
    LitModel -->|"contains"| AE
    
    UtilsViz -->|"reads"| AnnData
    UtilsViz -->|"reads"| LitModel
```

**Sources**: [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:1-545]()

### Module Overview

| Module | Primary Classes/Functions | Purpose | Reference |
|--------|--------------------------|---------|-----------|
| `src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py` | `AESTETIK` | Main orchestrator for training and prediction | [AESTETIK Class](#5.1) |
| `src/aestetik/data_modules/data_module.py` | `AESTETIKDataModule` | PyTorch Lightning DataModule for data loading | [Data Pipeline Components](#5.2) |
| `src/aestetik/utils/utils_data.py` | `prepare_input_for_model()`, `calibrate_weights()` | Input preprocessing and weight calibration | [Data Pipeline Components](#5.2) |
| `src/aestetik/utils/utils_grid.py` | `build_grid()`, `create_spot_grid()` | Spatial grid construction | [Data Pipeline Components](#5.2) |
| `src/aestetik/utils/utils_clustering.py` | `clustering()` | Clustering algorithms for transcriptomics and morphology | [Utility Functions](#5.4) |
| `src/aestetik/modules/aestetik_module.py` | `AESTETIKModel` | PyTorch Lightning module wrapper | [Model Architecture](#5.3) |
| `src/aestetik/models/ae.py` | `AE` | Autoencoder architecture | [Model Architecture](#5.3) |
| `src/aestetik/utils/utils_visualization.py` | `visualize()` | Plotting and visualization functions | [Utility Functions](#5.4) |

**Sources**: [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:1-545]()
