## Main Entry Point

The `AESTETIK` class provides the primary user-facing API. All interactions with the library typically go through this class.

### Core Methods

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "AESTETIK Class Methods"
        Init["__init__()<br/>Initialize with parameters"]
        Fit["fit()<br/>Train model on data"]
        Predict["predict()<br/>Generate embeddings"]
        FitPredict["fit_predict()<br/>Train and predict"]
        Version["version()<br/>Get version string"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Workflow Patterns"
        Pattern1["Pattern 1:<br/>Train then predict"]
        Pattern2["Pattern 2:<br/>Combined workflow"]
    end
    
    Init --> Fit
    Fit --> Predict
    Init --> FitPredict
    
    Fit -.->|"used in"| Pattern1
    Predict -.->|"used in"| Pattern1
    FitPredict -.->|"used in"| Pattern2
```

**Sources**: [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:24-545]()

### Method Signatures Summary

| Method | Parameters | Returns | Modifies AnnData | Purpose |
|--------|------------|---------|------------------|---------|
| `__init__()` | 26 configuration parameters | `AESTETIK` instance | No | Initialize model configuration |
| `fit()` | `X: AnnData`, obsm keys, validation split, early stopping | `None` | No | Train model on provided data |
| `predict()` | `X: AnnData`, obsm keys, num_repeats, cluster flag | `None` | Yes (adds to `obsm`, `obs`) | Generate embeddings and optionally cluster |
| `fit_predict()` | Combined parameters from fit and predict | `None` | Yes (adds to `obsm`, `obs`) | Train and predict in single call |
| `version()` | None | `str` | No | Return version string |

**Sources**: [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:29-545]()

### Instantiation Parameters

The `AESTETIK` class constructor accepts parameters organized into several categories:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Parameter Categories"
        ClusterParams["Clustering Parameters<br/>nCluster, clustering_method,<br/>n_neighbors, refine_cluster"]
        ModelParams["Model Architecture<br/>window_size, kernel_size,<br/>latent_dim, c_hid, p,<br/>n_ensemble, n_ensemble_encoder,<br/>n_ensemble_decoder"]
        LossParams["Loss & Regularization<br/>morphology_weight, total_weight,<br/>rec_alpha, triplet_alpha,<br/>multi_triplet_loss, n_repeats"]
        TrainingParams["Training Configuration<br/>lr, weight_decay, max_epochs,<br/>batch_size, num_workers"]
        DataParams["Data Handling<br/>train_size, n_jobs,<br/>random_seed"]
    end
    
    Init["AESTETIK.__init__()"]
    
    ClusterParams --> Init
    ModelParams --> Init
    LossParams --> Init
    TrainingParams --> Init
    DataParams --> Init
```

**Sources**: [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:29-173]()

#### Parameter Storage Structure

Parameters are internally organized into dictionaries for modular access:

| Internal Dictionary | Parameters Stored | Used By |
|---------------------|------------------|---------|
| `grid_params` | `morphology_dim`, `num_input_channels`, `obsm_transcriptomics_dim` | Grid construction, model input layer |
| `model_architecture_params` | `latent_dim`, `c_hid`, `kernel_size`, `p`, `n_ensemble_encoder`, `n_ensemble_decoder` | `AE` architecture initialization |
| `dataloader_params` | `batch_size`, `num_workers` | PyTorch DataLoader configuration |
| `training_params` | `lr`, `weight_decay`, `max_epochs` | Optimizer and Trainer configuration |
| `clustering_params` | `nCluster`, `clustering_method`, `n_neighbors`, `refine_cluster` | Clustering operations |
| `loss_regularization_params` | `multi_triplet_loss`, `rec_alpha`, `triplet_alpha`, `n_repeats`, `morphology_weight`, `transcriptomics_weight`, `total_weight` | Loss computation |
| `data_handling_params` | `n_jobs`, `train_size` | Data preprocessing |

**Sources**: [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:120-166]()

## Data Flow Through API Methods

The following diagram shows how data flows through the public API methods and which components are invoked at each stage.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant AESTETIK
    participant Validation["_validate_*_inputs()"]
    participant DataModule["AESTETIKDataModule"]
    participant Model["AESTETIKModel"]
    participant Trainer["lightning.Trainer"]
    
    Note over User,Trainer: fit() workflow
    User->>AESTETIK: fit(adata)
    AESTETIK->>Validation: _validate_fit_inputs()
    AESTETIK->>AESTETIK: _set_fit_params()
    AESTETIK->>DataModule: initialize
    AESTETIK->>Model: _build_model()
    AESTETIK->>Trainer: fit(model, datamodule)
    Trainer-->>AESTETIK: trained model
    
    Note over User,Trainer: predict() workflow
    User->>AESTETIK: predict(adata)
    AESTETIK->>AESTETIK: _check_fitted()
    AESTETIK->>Validation: _validate_predict_inputs()
    AESTETIK->>AESTETIK: _compute_latent_space()
    AESTETIK->>AESTETIK: _postprocess_predictions()
    AESTETIK-->>User: None (adata modified)
```

**Sources**: [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:179-332]()

## AnnData Interface Conventions

AESTETIK follows `scanpy` ecosystem conventions for reading and writing to `AnnData` objects.

### Required Input Fields

| AnnData Location | Default Key | Alternative Keys | Data Type | Description |
|------------------|-------------|------------------|-----------|-------------|
| `adata.obsm` | `"X_pca_transcriptomics"` | User-specified via `used_obsm_transcriptomics` | `np.ndarray` | PCA-reduced transcriptomics features |
| `adata.obsm` | `"X_pca_morphology"` | User-specified via `used_obsm_morphology` | `np.ndarray` | PCA-reduced morphology features |
| `adata.obsm` | `"X_pca"` | User-specified via `used_obsm_combined` | `np.ndarray` | Combined features (used in `fit()` only) |
| `adata.obs` | `"x_array"` | Fixed | `float` | X spatial coordinates |
| `adata.obs` | `"y_array"` | Fixed | `float` | Y spatial coordinates |
| `adata.obs` | User-specified | Via `used_obs_batch` parameter | `str` or `int` | Sample/batch labels (optional) |

**Sources**: [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:181-205](), [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:240-266]()

### Output Fields Written by API

| Method | AnnData Location | Default Key | Data Type | Description |
|--------|------------------|-------------|-----------|-------------|
| `fit()` | Various internal | N/A | N/A | No direct modifications to input `adata` |
| `predict()` | `adata.obsm` | `"AESTETIK"` (configurable via `save_emb`) | `np.ndarray` | Latent space embeddings |
| `predict()` | `adata.obs` | `"AESTETIK_cluster"` | `str` or `int` | Cluster assignments (if `cluster=True`) |
| `predict()` | `adata.obsm` | `"X_st_grid"` | `np.ndarray` | Spatial grids (temporary, used during computation) |

**Sources**: [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:505-520]()

### Validation Methods

| Method | Purpose | Raises |
|--------|---------|--------|
| `_validate_fit_inputs()` | Validate presence of required obsm keys and obs columns for training | `KeyError` |
| `_validate_predict_inputs()` | Validate inputs and check dimensionality compatibility with fitted model | `KeyError`, `ValueError` |
| `_check_fitted()` | Verify that model has been fitted before prediction | `RuntimeError` |
| `_validate_obsm_keys()` | Generic validator for checking obsm key existence | `KeyError` |
| `_validate_obs_columns()` | Generic validator for checking obs column existence | `KeyError` |

**Sources**: [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:337-393]()

### PyTorch Lightning Integration Points

| AESTETIK Component | Lightning Component | Integration Method |
|--------------------|---------------------|-------------------|
| `AESTETIKDataModule` | `LightningDataModule` | Inherits from base class |
| `AESTETIKModel` | `LightningModule` | Inherits from base class |
| `AESTETIK.fit()` | `Trainer.fit()` | Instantiates and calls `Trainer` |

## Common Parameter Patterns

Several parameters appear across multiple methods and components. Understanding their consistent usage simplifies API navigation.

### Cross-Method Parameters

| Parameter | Appears In | Data Type | Purpose | Default |
|-----------|------------|-----------|---------|---------|
| `used_obsm_transcriptomics` | `fit()`, `predict()`, `fit_predict()` | `str` | Key for transcriptomics features in `adata.obsm` | `"X_pca_transcriptomics"` |
| `used_obsm_morphology` | `fit()`, `predict()`, `fit_predict()` | `str` | Key for morphology features in `adata.obsm` | `"X_pca_morphology"` |
| `used_obsm_combined` | `fit()`, `fit_predict()` | `str` | Key for combined features in `adata.obsm` | `"X_pca"` |
| `used_obs_batch` | `fit()`, `predict()`, `fit_predict()` | `Optional[str]` | Key for batch/sample labels in `adata.obs` | `None` |
| `validation_split` | `fit()`, `fit_predict()` | `float` | Proportion of data for validation | `0.0` |
| `num_repeats` | `predict()`, `fit_predict()` | `int` | Number of stochastic forward passes | `1000` |
| `cluster` | `predict()`, `fit_predict()` | `bool` | Whether to perform clustering | `True` |
| `save_emb` | `predict()`, `fit_predict()` | `str` | Key for saving embeddings in `adata.obsm` | `"AESTETIK"` |

**Sources**: [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:179-332]()

### Parameter Validation Rules

The API enforces several validation rules on parameters:

| Validation | Applied To | Condition | Error Type |
|------------|------------|-----------|------------|
| Odd integer check | `window_size` | Must be odd | `ValueError` |
| Fitted model check | `predict()` calls | Must call `fit()` first | `RuntimeError` |
| Dimensionality check | `predict()` inputs | Feature dimensions must be ≥ fitted dimensions | `ValueError` |
| Key existence | All `used_obsm_*` parameters | Must exist in `adata.obsm` | `KeyError` |
| Column existence | `x_array`, `y_array` | Must exist in `adata.obs` | `KeyError` |

**Sources**: [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:117-118](), [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:369-371](), [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:337-393]()

# AESTETIK Class

## Purpose and Scope

The `AESTETIK` class serves as the primary user-facing orchestrator for the entire AESTETIK library. It provides a scikit-learn-style API with `fit()`, `predict()`, and `fit_predict()` methods to train multi-modal autoencoders on spatial transcriptomics data and generate embeddings for downstream analysis. This class manages the complete workflow from data validation through model training to prediction and clustering, delegating to specialized subsystems while maintaining a clean, high-level interface.

For detailed information about the underlying model architecture, see [Model Architecture](#5.3). For data processing components, see [Data Pipeline Components](#5.2). For utility functions including visualization, see [Utility Functions](#5.4).

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:1-545]()

---

## Class Overview

### Location and Dependencies

The `AESTETIK` class is defined in [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:24-545]() and imports:

| Dependency | Purpose |
|------------|---------|
| `anndata.AnnData` | Primary data container for spatial transcriptomics |
| `lightning.pytorch.Trainer` | PyTorch Lightning training infrastructure |
| `AESTETIKDataModule` | Data loading and preprocessing |
| `AESTETIKModel` | Lightning module wrapping the autoencoder |
| `LossHistoryCallback`, `EarlyStopping`, `ModelCheckpoint` | Training callbacks |
| `clustering` from `utils_clustering` | Post-prediction clustering |
| `build_grid` from `utils_data` | Spatial grid construction |
| `fix_seed` from `utils_grid` | Reproducibility utilities |

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:1-22]()

## Initialization and Parameter Organization

### Constructor Signature

The `AESTETIK` class is initialized with [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:29-57]():

```python
def __init__(
    self,
    nCluster: Union[int, float],
    morphology_weight: float,
    total_weight: float = 3,
    rec_alpha: float = 1,
    triplet_alpha: float = 1,
    train_size: Optional[float] = None,
    window_size: int = 7,
    kernel_size: int = 3,
    latent_dim: int = 16,
    c_hid: int = 64,
    lr: float = 0.001,
    p: float = 0.3,
    max_epochs: int = 100,
    multi_triplet_loss: bool = True,
    n_repeats: int = 1,
    clustering_method: Literal["bgm", "kmeans", "louvain", "leiden"] = "bgm",
    batch_size: Optional[int] = None,
    n_ensemble: int = 3,
    n_ensemble_encoder: Optional[int] = None,
    n_ensemble_decoder: Optional[int] = None,
    random_seed: int = 2023,
    n_neighbors: int = 10,
    weight_decay: float = 1e-6,
    refine_cluster: bool = True,
    n_jobs: int = 1,
    num_workers: int = 0
)
```

### Internal Parameter Organization

Parameters are organized into six thematic dictionaries [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:120-166]():

```mermaid

        GridParams["grid_params"]

    end

    end

        ClusteringParams --> RefineCluster["refine_cluster"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Loss Configuration"
        LossParams --> MultiTriplet["multi_triplet_loss"]
        LossParams --> RecAlpha["rec_alpha"]
        LossParams --> TripletAlpha["triplet_alpha"]
        LossParams --> NRepeats["n_repeats"]
        LossParams --> MorphWeight["morphology_weight"]
        LossParams --> TransWeight["transcriptomics_weight: None (calibrated)"]
        LossParams --> TotalWeight["total_weight"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Data Handling"
        DataHandlingParams --> NJobs["n_jobs"]
        DataHandlingParams --> TrainSize["train_size"]
    end
    
    Init --> GridParams
    Init --> ModelParams
    Init --> DataLoaderParams
    Init --> TrainingParams
    Init --> ClusteringParams
    Init --> LossParams
    Init --> DataHandlingParams
```

**Key Design Principles:**

- **Deferred Initialization:** `num_input_channels` and `obsm_transcriptomics_dim` are set during `fit()` based on actual data dimensions
- **Adaptive Batch Size:** If `batch_size=None`, automatically set to `min(2**13, len(X))` at fit time
- **Ensemble Flexibility:** `n_ensemble` sets both encoder and decoder ensemble sizes unless overridden individually
- **Kernel Size Validation:** Automatically adjusted to `max(1, window_size - 1)` if provided `kernel_size >= window_size`

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:29-173]()

---

## Public API Methods

### fit() - Model Training

Trains the autoencoder model on spatial transcriptomics data [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:179-238]().

**Method Signature:**

```python
def fit(
    self, 
    X: anndata.AnnData,
    used_obsm_transcriptomics: str = "X_pca_transcriptomics",
    used_obsm_morphology: str = "X_pca_morphology",
    used_obsm_combined: str = "X_pca",
    used_obs_batch: Optional[str] = None,
    validation_split: float = 0.0,
    early_stopping_params: Optional[dict] = None
) -> None
```

**Parameters:**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Purpose |
|-----------|------|---------|---------|
| `X` | `anndata.AnnData` | Required | Input data with PCA features in `obsm` and spatial coordinates in `obs` |
| `used_obsm_transcriptomics` | `str` | `"X_pca_transcriptomics"` | Key for transcriptomics features in `X.obsm` |
| `used_obsm_morphology` | `str` | `"X_pca_morphology"` | Key for morphology features in `X.obsm` |
| `used_obsm_combined` | `str` | `"X_pca"` | Key for combined features in `X.obsm` |
| `used_obs_batch` | `Optional[str]` | `None` | Key for batch/sample labels in `X.obs` |
| `validation_split` | `float` | `0.0` | Proportion of data for validation (0.0 to 1.0) |
| `early_stopping_params` | `Optional[dict]` | `None` | Parameters for early stopping (`min_delta`, `patience`) |

**Required Data Format:**

The input `AnnData` object must contain:
- `X.obsm[used_obsm_transcriptomics]`: Transcriptomics PCA features (shape: `n_spots × n_pca_components`)
- `X.obsm[used_obsm_morphology]`: Morphology PCA features (shape: `n_spots × n_pca_components`)
- `X.obs["x_array"]`: Spatial x-coordinates
- `X.obs["y_array"]`: Spatial y-coordinates

**Workflow Diagram:**

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant fit["AESTETIK.fit()"]
    participant validate["_validate_fit_inputs()"]
    participant set_params["_set_fit_params()"]
    participant DataModule["AESTETIKDataModule"]
    participant build["_build_model()"]
    participant callbacks["_create_callbacks()"]
    participant Trainer["Lightning Trainer"]

    User->>fit: "fit(X, validation_split=0.1)"
    activate fit
    
    fit->>validate: "Check obsm keys & obs columns"
    validate-->>fit: "Validation passed"
    
    fit->>set_params: "Set batch_size, transcriptomics_dim"
    set_params-->>fit: "Parameters configured"
    
    fit->>DataModule: "Initialize with X and all params"
    activate DataModule
    DataModule->>DataModule: "prepare_input_for_model()"
    DataModule->>DataModule: "setup() - create train/val splits"
    DataModule-->>fit: "data_module ready"
    deactivate DataModule
    
    fit->>build: "_build_model(datamodule)"
    build-->>fit: "lit_aestetik_model (AESTETIKModel)"
    
    fit->>callbacks: "Create LossHistory, EarlyStopping, ModelCheckpoint"
    callbacks-->>fit: "callbacks list"
    
    fit->>Trainer: "Trainer(max_epochs, callbacks)"
    fit->>Trainer: "trainer.fit(model, datamodule)"
    activate Trainer
    Trainer->>Trainer: "Training loop over epochs"
    Trainer-->>fit: "Training complete"
    deactivate Trainer
    
    fit->>fit: "Store self.losses from callback"
    fit-->>User: "self (fitted)"
    deactivate fit
```

**Side Effects:**

- Sets `self.lit_aestetik_model` to the trained `AESTETIKModel` instance
- Sets `self.trainer` to the Lightning `Trainer` instance
- Sets `self.losses` with training history from `LossHistoryCallback`
- Updates `self.grid_params["obsm_transcriptomics_dim"]` based on actual data
- Updates `self.dataloader_params["batch_size"]` if it was `None`

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:179-238](), [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:337-367](), [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:398-408]()

---

### predict() - Generate Embeddings

Computes latent space embeddings for spots and optionally performs clustering [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:240-282]().

**Method Signature:**

```python
def predict(
    self,
    X: anndata.AnnData,
    used_obsm_transcriptomics: str = "X_pca_transcriptomics",
    used_obsm_morphology: str = "X_pca_morphology",
    used_obs_batch: Optional[str] = None,
    save_emb: str = "AESTETIK",
    num_repeats: int = 1000,
    cluster: bool = True
) -> None
```

**Parameters:**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Purpose |
|-----------|------|---------|---------|
| `X` | `anndata.AnnData` | Required | Input data (can be different from training data) |
| `used_obsm_transcriptomics` | `str` | `"X_pca_transcriptomics"` | Key for transcriptomics features |
| `used_obsm_morphology` | `str` | `"X_pca_morphology"` | Key for morphology features |
| `used_obs_batch` | `Optional[str]` | `None` | Key for batch labels |
| `save_emb` | `str` | `"AESTETIK"` | Key for storing embeddings in `X.obsm` |
| `num_repeats` | `int` | `1000` | Number of stochastic forward passes (Monte Carlo dropout) |
| `cluster` | `bool` | `True` | Whether to perform clustering on embeddings |

**Pre-Conditions:**

- `fit()` must have been called successfully (checked via `_check_fitted()`)
- Input dimensions must be compatible with trained model (validated via `_validate_predict_inputs()`)
- If dimensions exceed training dimensions, they are automatically trimmed via `_calibrate_predict_inputs()`

**Workflow Diagram:**

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant predict["AESTETIK.predict()"]
    participant check["_check_fitted()"]
    participant validate["_validate_predict_inputs()"]
    participant calibrate["_calibrate_predict_inputs()"]
    participant compute["_compute_latent_space()"]
    participant create_dl["_create_predict_dataloader()"]
    participant build_grid_fn["build_grid()"]
    participant Trainer["Lightning Trainer"]
    participant postprocess["_postprocess_predictions()"]
    participant clustering_fn["clustering()"]

    User->>predict: "predict(X, num_repeats=1000)"
    activate predict
    
    predict->>check: "Ensure model is fitted"
    check-->>predict: "trainer & model exist"
    
    predict->>validate: "Check dimensions & keys"
    validate->>calibrate: "Trim dimensions if needed"
    calibrate-->>validate: "Calibrated features"
    validate-->>predict: "Validation passed"
    
    predict->>predict: "_set_predict_params(num_repeats)"
    
    predict->>compute: "_compute_latent_space(X, ...)"
    activate compute
    
    compute->>create_dl: "Create DataLoader"
    create_dl->>build_grid_fn: "build_grid(X, window_size, ...)"
    build_grid_fn-->>create_dl: "X.obsm['X_st_grid'] created"
    create_dl-->>compute: "DataLoader ready"
    
    compute->>Trainer: "trainer.predict(model, dataloader)"
    activate Trainer
    Trainer->>Trainer: "Multiple forward passes per batch"
    Trainer-->>compute: "Averaged latent spaces"
    deactivate Trainer
    
    compute-->>predict: "all_latent_space tensor"
    deactivate compute
    
    predict->>postprocess: "_postprocess_predictions(...)"
    activate postprocess
    postprocess->>postprocess: "Store in X.obsm[save_emb]"
    
    alt "cluster=True"
        postprocess->>clustering_fn: "clustering(X, used_obsm=save_emb, ...)"
        clustering_fn-->>postprocess: "Clusters stored in X.obs"
    end
    
    postprocess-->>predict: "X modified in-place"
    deactivate postprocess
    
    predict-->>User: "None (X modified)"
    deactivate predict
```

**Outputs (Modified In-Place):**

- `X.obsm[save_emb]`: Latent space embeddings (shape: `n_spots × latent_dim`)
- If `cluster=True`:
  - `X.obs["cluster"]`: Cluster assignments
  - `X.obs["cluster_refined"]`: Spatially refined cluster assignments (if `refine_cluster=True`)

**Cross-Sample Prediction:**

The `predict()` method supports cross-sample prediction, allowing you to train on one sample and predict on another. The method automatically:
1. Validates dimensional compatibility
2. Calibrates input dimensions by trimming if necessary
3. Reconstructs spatial grids for the new data

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:240-282](), [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:345-426](), [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:489-520]()

---

### fit_predict() - Combined Training and Prediction

Convenience method that calls `fit()` followed by `predict()` on the same data [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:284-332]().

**Method Signature:**

```python
def fit_predict(
    self,
    X: anndata.AnnData,
    used_obsm_transcriptomics: str = "X_pca_transcriptomics",
    used_obsm_morphology: str = "X_pca_morphology",
    used_obsm_combined: str = "X_pca",
    used_obs_batch: Optional[str] = None,
    validation_split: float = 0.0,
    save_emb: str = "AESTETIK",
    num_repeats: int = 1000,
    cluster: bool = True
) -> None
```

**Key Optimization:**

Unlike calling `fit()` and then `predict()` separately, `fit_predict()` avoids rebuilding spatial grids by setting `built_grid=True` in the internal `_compute_latent_space()` call [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:326-327](). The spatial grids are already available in `X.obsm["X_st_grid"]` from the data module's preprocessing during `fit()`.

**Typical Usage Pattern:**

```python
# Single-step training and clustering
model = AESTETIK(nCluster=10, morphology_weight=1.0)
model.fit_predict(adata, num_repeats=1000)
# adata.obsm["AESTETIK"] now contains embeddings
# adata.obs["cluster"] now contains cluster assignments
```

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:284-332]()

## Internal State Management

### State Tracking Attributes

The `AESTETIK` class maintains the following instance attributes [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:169-171]():

| Attribute | Type | Purpose |
|-----------|------|---------|
| `lit_aestetik_model` | `Optional[AESTETIKModel]` | Trained Lightning module (set during `fit()`) |
| `trainer` | `Optional[Trainer]` | Lightning Trainer instance (set during `fit()`) |
| `losses` | - | Training loss history (set after `fit()`) |
| `random_seed` | `int` | Seed for reproducibility |

### State Validation

The `_check_fitted()` method [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:369-371]() ensures the model has been trained before prediction:

```python
def _check_fitted(self) -> None:
    if self.trainer is None or self.lit_aestetik_model is None:
        raise RuntimeError("The model has not been fitted yet. Call 'fit' before 'predict'.")
```

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:169-173](), [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:369-371]()

### Data Preparation Methods

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Data Preparation Pipeline"
        SetFitParams["_set_fit_params()"]
        SetPredictParams["_set_predict_params()"]
        CreatePredictDL["_create_predict_dataloader()"]
        CreateCallbacks["_create_callbacks()"]
        CreateEarlyStop["_create_early_stopping_params()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Configuration Tasks"
        SetFitParams --> Task1["Set batch_size if None"]
        SetFitParams --> Task2["Set obsm_transcriptomics_dim"]
        SetPredictParams --> Task3["Update model.predict_params"]
        CreatePredictDL --> Task4["Build grid if needed"]
        CreatePredictDL --> Task5["Create TensorDataset + DataLoader"]
        CreateCallbacks --> Task6["Add LossHistoryCallback"]
        CreateCallbacks --> Task7["Add EarlyStopping if val_split > 0"]
        CreateCallbacks --> Task8["Add ModelCheckpoint if val_split > 0"]
    end
```

**Method Descriptions:**

| Method | Lines | Purpose |
|--------|-------|---------|
| `_set_fit_params()` | [398-404]() | Configures batch size and records transcriptomics dimensionality |
| `_set_predict_params()` | [406-408]() | Updates model's `num_repeats` for stochastic prediction |
| `_calibrate_predict_inputs()` | [410-425]() | Trims feature dimensions to match training configuration |
| `_create_predict_dataloader()` | [428-447]() | Builds spatial grids and creates DataLoader for prediction |
| `_create_callbacks()` | [449-467]() | Assembles callbacks for training monitoring |
| `_create_early_stopping_params()` | [469-484]() | Configures early stopping with validation |

**Key Design Note:**

The `_create_predict_dataloader()` method accepts a `built_grid` parameter [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:433](). When `True`, it skips calling `build_grid()`, assuming `X.obsm["X_st_grid"]` already exists. This optimization is used by `fit_predict()` to avoid redundant computation.

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:395-484]()

### Prediction and Postprocessing Methods

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Prediction Pipeline"
        ComputeLatent["_compute_latent_space()"]
        Postprocess["_postprocess_predictions()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Latent Space Computation"
        ComputeLatent --> Step1["Create predict DataLoader"]
        Step1 --> Step2["trainer.predict()"]
        Step2 --> Step3["Concatenate batches"]
        Step3 --> Step4["Return tensor"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Postprocessing Tasks"
        Postprocess --> Save["Store in X.obsm[save_emb]"]
        Save --> CheckCluster["if cluster=True"]
        CheckCluster --> DoClustering["clustering()"]
        DoClustering --> StoreCluster["Store in X.obs"]
    end
    
    ComputeLatent --> Postprocess
```

**Method Descriptions:**

| Method | Lines | Purpose |
|--------|-------|---------|
| `_compute_latent_space()` | [489-503]() | Computes embeddings via stochastic forward passes |
| `_postprocess_predictions()` | [505-520]() | Stores embeddings and performs optional clustering |

**Stochastic Prediction Detail:**

The `num_repeats` parameter controls Monte Carlo dropout averaging. The model is run multiple times with dropout enabled during inference, and the latent representations are averaged. This is handled by the `AESTETIKModel.predict_step()` method, but orchestrated through the parameter set by `_set_predict_params()`.

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:486-520]()

---

### Model Construction

```mermaid
graph LR
    BuildModel["_build_model()"]
    
    subgraph "Parameter Assembly"
        BuildModel --> TrainParams["training_step_params"]
        BuildModel --> OptimParams["optimizer_step_params"]
        TrainParams --> RecAlpha["rec_alpha"]
        TrainParams --> TripletAlpha["triplet_alpha"]
        OptimParams --> LR["lr"]
        OptimParams --> WeightDecay["weight_decay"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Model Creation"
        BuildModel --> AESTETIKModel["AESTETIKModel(...)"]
        AESTETIKModel --> PassDataModule["datamodule"]
        AESTETIKModel --> PassGridParams["grid_params"]
        AESTETIKModel --> PassModelParams["model_architecture_params"]
        AESTETIKModel --> PassTrainParams["training_params"]
        AESTETIKModel --> PassOptimParams["optimizer_params"]
    end
```

The `_build_model()` method [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:525-541]() constructs the `AESTETIKModel` Lightning module by:

1. Extracting relevant parameters from internal dictionaries
2. Creating `training_step_params` with `rec_alpha` and `triplet_alpha`
3. Creating `optimizer_step_params` with `lr` and `weight_decay`
4. Instantiating `AESTETIKModel` with all configuration dictionaries

**Key Insight:** The `datamodule` is passed to the model constructor because it contains essential information about modality weights and loss configuration that was computed during data preprocessing.

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:522-541]()

```mermaid
    AESTETIKDataModule -->|"returns"| AESTETIK
    AESTETIKModel -->|"uses"| AESTETIKDataModule
    Trainer -->|"trains"| AESTETIKModel
    Trainer -->|"predicts with"| AESTETIKModel
    LossHistory -->|"tracks losses"| AESTETIK
```

### Key Integration Points

**Data Module Integration:**

The `AESTETIK` class delegates all data preprocessing to `AESTETIKDataModule` [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:217-227]():

```python
datamodule = AESTETIKDataModule(X,
    used_obsm_transcriptomics=used_obsm_transcriptomics,
    used_obsm_morphology=used_obsm_morphology,
    used_obsm_combined=used_obsm_combined,
    used_obs_batch=used_obs_batch,
    dataloader_params=self.dataloader_params,
    clustering_params=self.clustering_params,
    grid_params=self.grid_params,
    loss_regularization_params=self.loss_regularization_params,
    data_handling_params=self.data_handling_params,
    validation_split=validation_split)
```

The data module handles:
- Clustering both modalities to generate triplet loss labels
- Calibrating modality weights based on cluster quality
- Building spatial grids for all spots
- Creating train/validation splits
- Providing DataLoaders to the trainer

**Lightning Integration:**

The `AESTETIK` class uses PyTorch Lightning's `Trainer` for all model training and inference [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:234-237]():

```python
self.trainer = Trainer(max_epochs=self.training_params["max_epochs"],
                       callbacks=callbacks,
                       num_sanity_val_steps=0)
self.trainer.fit(self.lit_aestetik_model, datamodule=datamodule)
```

For prediction [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:500-502]():

```python
all_latent_space = self.trainer.predict(self.lit_aestetik_model,
                                        dataloaders=predict_dataloader)
```

**Callback Integration:**

Three types of callbacks are managed:

1. **LossHistoryCallback** (always used): Tracks training and validation losses [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:454-455]()
2. **EarlyStopping** (when `validation_split > 0`): Monitors `val_loss` [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:459]()
3. **ModelCheckpoint** (when `validation_split > 0`): Saves best model [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:460-465]()

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:217-238](), [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:449-467](), [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:500-502](), [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:525-541]()

---

## Parameter Passing Flow

The following table shows how initialization parameters flow through the system:

| Parameter Group | Destination Component | Usage |
|----------------|----------------------|-------|
| `grid_params` | `AESTETIKDataModule` | Controls spatial grid construction via `utils_grid` |
| `grid_params` | `AESTETIKModel` | Defines input shape for autoencoder |
| `model_architecture_params` | `AESTETIKModel` | Configures encoder/decoder architecture |
| `dataloader_params` | `AESTETIKDataModule` | Configures DataLoader (batch size, workers) |
| `training_params` | `Lightning Trainer` | Sets `max_epochs` |
| `training_params` (lr, weight_decay) | `AESTETIKModel` optimizer | Configures Adam optimizer |
| `clustering_params` | `AESTETIKDataModule` | Initial clustering for triplet loss labels |
| `clustering_params` | `utils_clustering.clustering()` | Post-prediction clustering |
| `loss_regularization_params` | `AESTETIKDataModule` | Weight calibration and loss configuration |
| `loss_regularization_params` | `AESTETIKModel` | Computes weighted multi-component loss |
| `data_handling_params` | `AESTETIKDataModule` | Parallel grid construction, train/val split |

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:120-166](), [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:217-227](), [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:525-541]()

---

```python
@staticmethod
def version():
    return "16.06.2025:1"
```

This version identifier follows the format `DD.MM.YYYY:incrementalVersion`.

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/AESTETIK.py:543-545]()

## API Evolution

### Removed Methods (June 2025)

The following methods were removed to simplify the API:

| Old Method | Replacement | Notes |
|------------|-------------|-------|
| `summary()` | N/A | Removed |
| `prepare_input_for_model()` | Integrated into `fit()` | Now handled by `AESTETIKDataModule` |
| `train()` | `fit()` | Renamed for sklearn compatibility |
| `compute_spot()` | `predict()` | Renamed for sklearn compatibility |
| `vizualize()` | `visualize()` | Fixed typo and moved to `utils_visualization.py` |

### Removed Initialization Parameters

The following parameters are no longer passed to `__init__()` but instead to the methods that use them:

- `adata`: Now passed to `fit()` and `predict()`
- `device`: Auto-detected by PyTorch Lightning
- `used_obsm_transcriptomics`, `used_obsm_morphology`, `used_obsm_combined`: Now passed to `fit()` and `predict()`
- `save_emb`: Now passed to `predict()` and `fit_predict()`
- `img_path`, `spot_diameter_fullres`: Removed (visualization now in separate module)

**Rationale:** This change enables:
- **Cross-sample training and prediction:** Train on one sample, predict on another
- **Multi-sample support:** Train and predict across multiple samples
- **Cleaner separation of concerns:** Model configuration separate from data and runtime parameters

**Sources:** [CHANGELOG.md:1-39]()

# Page: Data Pipeline Components

# Data Pipeline Components

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/aestetik/data_modules/data_module.py](src/aestetik/data_modules/data_module.py)
- [src/aestetik/utils/utils_data.py](src/aestetik/utils/utils_data.py)
- [src/aestetik/utils/utils_grid.py](src/aestetik/utils/utils_grid.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This page provides technical reference documentation for the data pipeline components that prepare spatial transcriptomics data for model training. The pipeline transforms raw AnnData objects into batched spatial grid tensors suitable for the autoencoder architecture.

This document covers:
- `AESTETIKDataModule`: PyTorch Lightning DataModule for data orchestration
- Data preparation utilities in `utils_data.py`: clustering, weight calibration, and preprocessing coordination
- Spatial grid construction in `utils_grid.py`: KDTree-based neighborhood feature extraction

For information about the main AESTETIK orchestrator class that initializes these components, see [AESTETIK Class](#5.1). For details about the model architecture that consumes the prepared data, see [Model Architecture](#5.3). For clustering algorithms used in preprocessing, see [Utility Functions](#5.4).

---

## Component Overview

The data pipeline consists of three primary layers that transform raw spatial omics data into training-ready batches:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Layer 1: Orchestration"
        DataModule["AESTETIKDataModule<br/>(L.LightningDataModule)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Layer 2: Preprocessing Coordination"
        PrepareInput["prepare_input_for_model()"]
        BuildGrid["build_grid()"]
        Calibrate["calibrate_transcriptomics_<br/>morphology_ratio()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Layer 3: Spatial Grid Construction"
        CreateSTGrid["create_st_grid()"]
        BuildTrees["_build_trees()"]
        CreateBatchGrid["_create_batch_grid()"]
        CreateSpot["_create_spot()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "External Dependencies"
        Clustering["clustering()<br/>(utils_clustering)"]
        CustomDS["CustomDataset<br/>(dataloader.py)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Input/Output"
        Input["AnnData<br/>Raw Features"]
        Output["DataLoader<br/>Batched Grids"]
    end
    
    Input --> DataModule
    DataModule --> PrepareInput
    PrepareInput --> Clustering
    PrepareInput --> Calibrate
    PrepareInput --> BuildGrid
    BuildGrid --> CreateSTGrid
    CreateSTGrid --> BuildTrees
    CreateSTGrid --> CreateBatchGrid
    CreateBatchGrid --> CreateSpot
    DataModule --> CustomDS
    CustomDS --> Output
    
    style DataModule fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style PrepareInput fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style CreateSTGrid fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
```

**Sources**: [src/aestetik/data_modules/data_module.py:1-159](), [src/aestetik/utils/utils_data.py:1-112](), [src/aestetik/utils/utils_grid.py:1-188]()

## AESTETIKDataModule Class

### Class Definition

`AESTETIKDataModule` is a PyTorch Lightning DataModule that orchestrates the complete data preparation pipeline and provides dataloaders for training and validation.

**File Location**: [src/aestetik/data_modules/data_module.py:12-159]()

### Initialization Parameters

The class is initialized with structured parameter dictionaries:

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `adata` | `anndata.AnnData` | Input AnnData object containing transcriptomics and morphology features |
| `validation_split` | `float` | Proportion of data for validation (0.0 to 1.0) |
| `used_obsm_transcriptomics` | `str` | Key in `adata.obsm` for transcriptomics features (e.g., PCA) |
| `used_obsm_morphology` | `str` | Key in `adata.obsm` for morphology features |
| `used_obsm_combined` | `str` | Key to store concatenated features |
| `used_obs_batch` | `Optional[str]` | Key in `adata.obs` for batch labels (for multi-sample data) |
| `dataloader_params` | `dict` | Contains `batch_size`, `num_workers` |
| `clustering_params` | `dict` | Contains `nCluster`, `clustering_method`, `n_neighbors` |
| `grid_params` | `dict` | Contains `morphology_dim` (window size) |
| `loss_regularization_params` | `dict` | Contains `multi_triplet_loss`, `n_repeats`, `morphology_weight`, `transcriptomics_weight`, `total_weight` |
| `data_handling_params` | `dict` | Contains `n_jobs`, `train_size` |

**Sources**: [src/aestetik/data_modules/data_module.py:13-93]()

### Key Methods

#### setup()

The `setup()` method triggers the complete preprocessing pipeline:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant DM as "DataModule.setup()"
    participant Prep as "prepare_input_for_model()"
    participant CDS as "CustomDataset"
    participant Split as "random_split()"
    
    DM->>Prep: "Pass all parameters"
    Note over Prep: "1. Cluster transcriptomics"
    Note over Prep: "2. Cluster morphology"
    Note over Prep: "3. Calibrate weights"
    Note over Prep: "4. Build spatial grids"
    Prep-->>DM: "Return adjusted weights"
    
    DM->>CDS: "Create dataset with grids"
    Note over CDS: "Stores X_st_grid from obsm"
    
    alt "validation_split > 0"
        DM->>Split: "Split into train/val"
        Split-->>DM: "train_dataset, val_dataset"
    else "validation_split == 0"
        Note over DM: "Use all data for training"
    end
```

**Sources**: [src/aestetik/data_modules/data_module.py:96-134]()

**Key Operations**:
1. Calls `prepare_input_for_model()` with all configuration parameters [line 98-108]()
2. Receives calibrated `transcriptomics_weight` and `morphology_weight` [line 98]()
3. Creates `CustomDataset` instance with processed data [line 109-114]()
4. Splits dataset into training and validation sets if `validation_split > 0` [line 116-134]()

#### train_dataloader()

Returns a PyTorch DataLoader for training data:

```python
# Returns: torch.utils.data.DataLoader
# Configuration: uses self.dataloader_params (batch_size, num_workers)
# Shuffle: True
```

**Sources**: [src/aestetik/data_modules/data_module.py:137-140]()

#### val_dataloader()

Returns a PyTorch DataLoader for validation data, or empty iterator if no validation split:

```python
# Returns: torch.utils.data.DataLoader or empty iterator
# Configuration: uses self.dataloader_params
# Shuffle: False
```

**Sources**: [src/aestetik/data_modules/data_module.py:142-145]()

#### _validate_params()

Validates that all required parameter keys are present in the configuration dictionaries:

| Dictionary | Required Keys |
|------------|---------------|
| `dataloader_params` | `batch_size`, `num_workers` |
| `clustering_params` | `nCluster`, `clustering_method`, `n_neighbors` |
| `grid_params` | `morphology_dim` |
| `loss_regularization_params` | `multi_triplet_loss`, `n_repeats`, `morphology_weight`, `transcriptomics_weight` |
| `data_handling_params` | `n_jobs`, `train_size` |

**Sources**: [src/aestetik/data_modules/data_module.py:147-159]()

## Data Preparation Functions (utils_data.py)

### prepare_input_for_model()

**Function Signature**: [src/aestetik/utils/utils_data.py:14-72]()

The main preprocessing orchestrator that coordinates clustering, weight calibration, and grid construction.

**Preprocessing Pipeline**:

```mermaid
graph TD
    Start["Input: AnnData with<br/>transcriptomics & morphology<br/>in adata.obsm"]
    
    ClusterT["clustering()<br/>transcriptomics modality"]
    ClusterM["clustering()<br/>morphology modality"]
    
    Calibrate["calibrate_transcriptomics_<br/>morphology_ratio()"]
    
    Concat["Concatenate modalities<br/>into used_obsm_combined"]
    
    BuildG["build_grid()<br/>Create spatial grids"]
    
    End["Output: Adjusted weights<br/>Grid stored in adata.obsm"]
    
    Start --> ClusterT
    Start --> ClusterM
    ClusterT --> Calibrate
    ClusterM --> Calibrate
    Calibrate --> Concat
    Concat --> BuildG
    BuildG --> End
```

**Sources**: [src/aestetik/utils/utils_data.py:14-72]()

**Parameters**:
- `adata`: AnnData object to preprocess
- `nCluster`: Number of clusters (int) or resolution (float)
- `used_obsm_transcriptomics`: Key for transcriptomics features in `adata.obsm`
- `used_obsm_morphology`: Key for morphology features in `adata.obsm`
- `used_obsm_combined`: Key to store concatenated features
- `clustering_method`: One of `"bgm"`, `"kmeans"`, `"louvain"`, `"leiden"`
- `n_neighbors`: Number of neighbors for spatial cluster refinement
- `window_size`: Grid window dimension (e.g., 5 for 5×5 grids)
- `n_jobs`: Number of parallel jobs for grid construction
- `total_weight`: Total loss weight across modalities
- `morphology_weight`: Initial weight for morphology modality
- `used_obs_batch`: Optional batch column key in `adata.obs`

**Returns**: 
- `transcriptomics_weight`: Calibrated weight for transcriptomics (may be 0 if clustering failed)
- `morphology_weight`: Calibrated weight for morphology (may be 0 if clustering failed)

**Side Effects**:
- Stores cluster labels in `adata.obs[f"{used_obsm}_cluster"]` for each modality [lines 35-51]()
- Creates concatenated features in `adata.obsm[used_obsm_combined]` [lines 62-63]()
- Stores spatial grids in `adata.obsm["X_st_grid"]` via `build_grid()` [lines 65-70]()

### build_grid()

**Function Signature**: [src/aestetik/utils/utils_data.py:74-89]()

Coordinates spatial grid construction for both modalities and concatenates results.

**Processing Flow**:

```mermaid
graph LR
    Trans["Transcriptomics<br/>Features"]
    Morph["Morphology<br/>Features"]
    
    GridT["create_st_grid()<br/>Transcriptomics Grid"]
    GridM["create_st_grid()<br/>Morphology Grid"]
    
    Concat["np.concatenate()<br/>axis=1"]
    
    Store["adata.obsm['X_st_grid']"]
    
    Trans --> GridT
    Morph --> GridM
    GridT --> Concat
    GridM --> Concat
    Concat --> Store
```

**Sources**: [src/aestetik/utils/utils_data.py:74-89]()

**Key Operations**:
1. Calls `create_st_grid()` for transcriptomics features [lines 81-82]()
2. Calls `create_st_grid()` for morphology features [lines 85-86]()
3. Concatenates grids along channel axis [lines 88-89]()
4. Final shape: `(n_spots, transcriptomics_dim + morphology_dim, window_size, window_size)`

### calibrate_transcriptomics_morphology_ratio()

**Function Signature**: [src/aestetik/utils/utils_data.py:91-112]()

Adjusts modality weights when clustering fails to produce the expected number of clusters.

**Calibration Logic**:

```mermaid
graph TD
    Start["Input: Initial weights<br/>and cluster results"]
    
    CheckT{"Transcriptomics<br/>resulted in<br/>1 cluster?"}
    CheckM{"Morphology<br/>resulted in<br/>1 cluster?"}
    
    SetT["Set transcriptomics_weight = 0"]
    SetM["Set morphology_weight = 0"]
    
    Keep["Keep original weights"]
    
    End["Return adjusted weights"]
    
    Start --> CheckT
    CheckT -->|"Yes & weight > 0"| SetT
    CheckT -->|"No"| CheckM
    SetT --> CheckM
    
    CheckM -->|"Yes & weight > 0"| SetM
    CheckM -->|"No"| Keep
    SetM --> End
    Keep --> End
```

**Sources**: [src/aestetik/utils/utils_data.py:91-112]()

**Rationale**: When a modality produces only 1 cluster instead of the requested `nCluster`, it indicates the features are not discriminative for spatial domain identification. Setting the weight to 0 prevents this modality from contributing to triplet loss, allowing the other modality to guide learning.

**Implementation Details**:
- Checks if `adata.obs[f"{used_obsm}_cluster"].unique().size == 1` [lines 101, 107]()
- Sets weight to 0 if condition is met and original weight was positive [lines 103-104, 109-110]()
- Logs weight adjustments for transparency [lines 102-103, 108-109]()

---

## Spatial Grid Construction (utils_grid.py)

### create_st_grid()

**Function Signature**: [src/aestetik/utils/utils_grid.py:54-108]()

Constructs spatial grids for all spots using KDTree-based neighbor queries and parallel processing.

**Architecture Overview**:

```mermaid
graph TB
    Input["Input:<br/>adata.obsm[used_obsm]<br/>adata.obs['x_array', 'y_array']"]
    
    Scale["MinMaxScaler<br/>Scale features to [0,1]"]
    
    Batch["Build KDTrees per batch<br/>_build_trees()"]
    
    Parallel["Parallel processing<br/>Split spots across n_jobs"]
    
    CreateBatch["_create_batch_grid()<br/>Process spot subset"]
    
    CreateSpot["_create_spot()<br/>Per-spot grid construction"]
    
    Concat["Concatenate results<br/>Reshape to (N,C,H,W)"]
    
    Output["Output:<br/>np.ndarray<br/>(n_spots, dim, window_size, window_size)"]
    
    Input --> Scale
    Scale --> Batch
    Batch --> Parallel
    Parallel --> CreateBatch
    CreateBatch --> CreateSpot
    CreateSpot --> Concat
    Concat --> Output
```

**Sources**: [src/aestetik/utils/utils_grid.py:54-108]()

**Key Processing Steps**:

1. **Feature Scaling** [lines 64-65]():
   - Applies `MinMaxScaler` with range `(0, 1)` to all features
   - Ensures consistent feature magnitudes across modalities

2. **Batch Handling** [lines 69-80]():
   - Extracts `used_obs_batch` column if specified
   - Converts to categorical codes for efficient indexing
   - Treats all data as single batch if no batch column exists

3. **KDTree Construction** [lines 78-80]():
   - Calls `_build_trees()` to create spatial indices per batch
   - Returns `trees` dict and `batch_to_indices` mapping

4. **Offset Computation** [lines 82-83]():
   - Calls `_compute_offsets_flat()` to generate grid position offsets
   - For `window_size=5`, creates 25 (x,y) offsets from center

5. **Parallel Processing** [lines 91-105]():
   - Splits spots into `cpu_count` chunks
   - Uses `joblib.Parallel` with `prefer="threads"`
   - Passes immutable (write-protected) arrays to workers [lines 85-89]()

6. **Grid Assembly** [lines 106-107]():
   - Concatenates spot grids from all workers
   - Reshapes from `(N, H, W, C)` to `(N, C, H, W)` using `np.moveaxis()`

**Return Shape**: `(num_spots, dim_emb, window_size, window_size)`

### _build_trees()

**Function Signature**: [src/aestetik/utils/utils_grid.py:110-123]()

Creates KDTree spatial indices for efficient neighbor queries, handling multi-batch data.

**Per-Batch Processing**:

```mermaid
graph TD
    BatchLabels["Input: batch_labels<br/>(one per spot)"]
    
    UniqueBatches["Extract unique batch IDs"]
    
    Loop["For each batch_id"]
    
    Filter["Filter spots:<br/>spot_indices = where(batch_labels == batch_id)"]
    
    Stack["Stack coordinates:<br/>np.column_stack([x_array, y_array])"]
    
    BuildTree["KDTree(coords)"]
    
    Store["trees[batch_id] = tree<br/>batch_to_indices[batch_id] = spot_indices"]
    
    BatchLabels --> UniqueBatches
    UniqueBatches --> Loop
    Loop --> Filter
    Filter --> Stack
    Stack --> BuildTree
    BuildTree --> Store
    Store --> Loop
```

**Sources**: [src/aestetik/utils/utils_grid.py:110-123]()

**Purpose**: Separating batches ensures spots from different tissue samples or experimental batches don't query neighbors across batch boundaries, preserving spatial coherence within each sample.

### _create_batch_grid()

**Function Signature**: [src/aestetik/utils/utils_grid.py:125-146]()

Processes a subset of spots assigned to a single parallel worker.

**Implementation**:
- Iterates over assigned `spot_indices` [line 135]()
- Calls `_create_spot()` for each spot [lines 136-144]()
- Collects results in list for efficient concatenation [line 145]()

**Sources**: [src/aestetik/utils/utils_grid.py:125-146]()

### _create_spot()

**Function Signature**: [src/aestetik/utils/utils_grid.py:148-182]()

Constructs the spatial feature grid for a single spot using neighbor queries and median imputation.

**Grid Construction Algorithm**:

```mermaid
graph TD
    Start["Input: spot_idx, spatial coords, features"]
    
    Init["Initialize grid:<br/>np.full((H, W, C), np.nan)"]
    
    GetBatch["Extract batch_id for spot"]
    
    GetTree["Get KDTree for this batch"]
    
    Loop["For each offset (dx, dy)"]
    
    Query["Query position = center + offset<br/>using tree.query()"]
    
    CheckDist{"distance > 0?"}
    
    Skip["Continue to next offset"]
    
    Place["Place neighbor features<br/>in grid[row, col]"]
    
    Median["Compute median across grid<br/>for each feature"]
    
    Impute["Fill NaN positions<br/>with median values"]
    
    End["Return completed grid"]
    
    Start --> Init
    Init --> GetBatch
    GetBatch --> GetTree
    GetTree --> Loop
    Loop --> Query
    Query --> CheckDist
    CheckDist -->|"Yes (no exact match)"| Skip
    CheckDist -->|"No (exact match)"| Place
    Skip --> Loop
    Place --> Loop
    Loop --> Median
    Median --> Impute
    Impute --> End
```

**Sources**: [src/aestetik/utils/utils_grid.py:148-182]()

**Key Implementation Details**:

1. **Grid Initialization** [lines 163-165]():
   - Shape: `(window_size, window_size, dim_emb)`
   - Filled with `np.nan` to track missing positions

2. **Neighbor Query** [lines 168-172]():
   - Computes target position: `center + [dx_offset, dy_offset]`
   - Uses `tree.query(position)` to find nearest neighbor
   - Only accepts exact matches (`distance == 0`)
   - Skips positions without exact coordinate matches

3. **Median Imputation** [lines 178-180]():
   - Computes `np.nanmedian(grid, axis=(0, 1))` across spatial dimensions
   - Replaces all `NaN` entries with corresponding feature medians
   - Ensures complete grids even for edge spots with fewer neighbors

**Rationale for Distance Threshold**: The strict `distance > 0` check [line 171]() ensures only spots at exact grid positions are included, preserving the regular spatial lattice structure typical of spatial transcriptomics platforms.

### _compute_offsets_flat()

**Function Signature**: [src/aestetik/utils/utils_grid.py:184-188]()

Generates flattened (x, y) offset arrays for grid positions.

**Example for window_size=5**:
```python
# start = -2, end = 3
# Returns shape (25, 2):
[[-2, -2], [-2, -1], [-2, 0], [-2, 1], [-2, 2],
 [-1, -2], [-1, -1], [-1, 0], [-1, 1], [-1, 2],
 ...
 [2, -2], [2, -1], [2, 0], [2, 1], [2, 2]]
```

**Sources**: [src/aestetik/utils/utils_grid.py:184-188]()

---

## Data Flow Integration

### Complete Pipeline Data Flow

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Input Stage"
        A["AnnData Object<br/>adata.obsm['X_pca_transcriptomics']<br/>adata.obsm['X_pca_morphology']<br/>adata.obs['x_array', 'y_array']"]
    end
    
    subgraph "AESTETIKDataModule.__init__()"
        B["Store parameters:<br/>- used_obsm keys<br/>- clustering_params<br/>- grid_params<br/>- loss_regularization_params"]
    end
    
    subgraph "DataModule.setup()"
        C["prepare_input_for_model()"]
        
        C1["clustering()<br/>for transcriptomics"]
        C2["clustering()<br/>for morphology"]
        C3["calibrate_transcriptomics_<br/>morphology_ratio()"]
        C4["build_grid()"]
        
        C4a["create_st_grid()<br/>for transcriptomics"]
        C4b["create_st_grid()<br/>for morphology"]
        
        C4a1["MinMaxScaler"]
        C4a2["_build_trees()"]
        C4a3["_create_batch_grid()"]
        C4a4["_create_spot()"]
        
        D["CustomDataset()"]
        E["random_split()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output Stage"
        F["train_dataloader()"]
        G["val_dataloader()"]
        H["Batched Tensors<br/>(N, C, H, W)"]
    end
    
    A --> B
    B --> C
    C --> C1
    C --> C2
    C1 --> C3
    C2 --> C3
    C3 --> C4
    C4 --> C4a
    C4 --> C4b
    C4a --> C4a1
    C4a1 --> C4a2
    C4a2 --> C4a3
    C4a3 --> C4a4
    C4b --> C4a1
    C4a --> D
    C4b --> D
    D --> E
    E --> F
    E --> G
    F --> H
    G --> H
    
    style A fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style C fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style D fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style H fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
```

**Sources**: [src/aestetik/data_modules/data_module.py:1-159](), [src/aestetik/utils/utils_data.py:1-112](), [src/aestetik/utils/utils_grid.py:1-188]()

### Key Data Transformations

| Stage | Input Shape | Output Shape | Storage Location |
|-------|-------------|--------------|------------------|
| Raw Features | `(n_spots, n_features)` | - | `adata.obsm[used_obsm_*]` |
| Clustering | - | `(n_spots,)` | `adata.obs[f"{used_obsm}_cluster"]` |
| Feature Scaling | `(n_spots, n_features)` | `(n_spots, n_features)` | In-memory |
| create_st_grid() | `(n_spots, n_features)` | `(n_spots, n_features, H, W)` | In-memory |
| Concatenate Grids | 2×`(n_spots, n_features, H, W)` | `(n_spots, 2*n_features, H, W)` | `adata.obsm["X_st_grid"]` |
| CustomDataset | - | `(batch_size, 2*n_features, H, W)` | DataLoader batches |

### Memory and Performance Considerations

**Parallelization**:
- Grid construction uses `joblib.Parallel` with `prefer="threads"` [line 94-95]()
- Number of workers controlled by `n_jobs` parameter
- Arrays are made read-only before parallel processing [lines 85-89]()

**Memory Efficiency**:
- Uses `np.float32` for features to reduce memory footprint [line 23]()
- Processes spots in chunks for parallel workers
- KDTree provides O(log n) neighbor queries vs O(n) brute force

**Batch Processing**:
- Separate KDTrees per batch prevent cross-batch neighbor queries
- Enables processing of multi-sample datasets
- Maintains spatial coherence within each tissue section

**Sources**: [src/aestetik/utils/utils_grid.py:29-108]()

---

## Usage Example

```python
from aestetik.data_modules.data_module import AESTETIKDataModule
import anndata as ad

# Load preprocessed AnnData with PCA features
adata = ad.read_h5ad("spatial_data.h5ad")

# Configure data module
data_module = AESTETIKDataModule(
    adata=adata,
    validation_split=0.1,
    used_obsm_transcriptomics="X_pca_transcriptomics",
    used_obsm_morphology="X_pca_morphology", 
    used_obsm_combined="X_pca_combined",
    used_obs_batch="batch_id",
    dataloader_params={"batch_size": 32, "num_workers": 4},
    clustering_params={"nCluster": 10, "clustering_method": "leiden", "n_neighbors": 15},
    grid_params={"morphology_dim": 5},
    loss_regularization_params={
        "multi_triplet_loss": True,
        "n_repeats": 3,
        "morphology_weight": 1.0,
        "transcriptomics_weight": None,  # Will be calibrated
        "total_weight": 2.0
    },
    data_handling_params={"n_jobs": 8, "train_size": None}
)

# Trigger preprocessing
data_module.setup(stage="fit")

# Access processed data
train_loader = data_module.train_dataloader()
val_loader = data_module.val_dataloader()

# Check results stored in AnnData
print(adata.obs.columns)  # Contains cluster labels
print(adata.obsm["X_st_grid"].shape)  # (n_spots, 2*dim, 5, 5)
```

**Sources**: [src/aestetik/data_modules/data_module.py:12-159]()

# Page: Model Architecture

# Model Architecture

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/aestetik/callbacks/callbacks.py](src/aestetik/callbacks/callbacks.py)
- [src/aestetik/metrics/loss_function.py](src/aestetik/metrics/loss_function.py)
- [src/aestetik/models/model.py](src/aestetik/models/model.py)
- [src/aestetik/modules/aestetik_module.py](src/aestetik/modules/aestetik_module.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This page documents the neural network model architecture used in AESTETIK, including the `AESTETIKModel` Lightning module wrapper and the `AE` autoencoder. This covers the convolutional encoder-decoder architecture, ensemble mechanisms, and loss computation.

For information about the AESTETIK orchestrator class that manages model training, see [AESTETIK Class](#5.1). For data preprocessing and batch creation, see [Data Pipeline Components](#5.2).

---

## Component Overview

The model architecture consists of three primary components:

| Component | Class | File | Purpose |
|-----------|-------|------|---------|
| Lightning Wrapper | `AESTETIKModel` | `aestetik_module.py` | PyTorch Lightning module handling training loops, optimization, and prediction |
| Core Model | `AE` | `model.py` | Convolutional autoencoder with ensemble encoder/decoder |
| Loss Computation | `compute_loss()` | `loss_function.py` | Multi-component loss function for reconstruction and triplet losses |

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/modules/aestetik_module.py:1-185](), [src/aestetik/models/model.py:1-98](), [src/aestetik/metrics/loss_function.py:1-90]()

---

## Module Class Hierarchy

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class LightningModule {
        <<PyTorch Lightning>>
    }
    
    class AESTETIKModel {
        +datamodule: AESTETIKDataModule
        +model: AE
        +loss: dict
        +weights: dict
        +predict_params: dict
        +setup()
        +configure_model()
        +training_step()
        +validation_step()
        +predict_step()
        +configure_optimizers()
    }
    
    class AE {
        +encoder_ensemble: ModuleList
        +decoder_ensemble: ModuleList
        +encoder()
        +decoder()
        +forward()
    }
    
    class Encode {
        +encoder: Sequential
        +forward()
    }
    
    class Decode {
        +decoder: Sequential
        +forward()
    }
    
    class Module {
        <<PyTorch>>
    }
    
    LightningModule <|-- AESTETIKModel
    Module <|-- AE
    Module <|-- Encode
    Module <|-- Decode
    AESTETIKModel --> AE : contains
    AE --> Encode : ensemble
    AE --> Decode : ensemble
```

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/modules/aestetik_module.py:14-21](), [src/aestetik/models/model.py:51-98]()

---

## AESTETIKModel Lightning Module

The `AESTETIKModel` class extends `lightning.LightningModule` and serves as the training orchestrator. It wraps the core `AE` autoencoder and implements PyTorch Lightning's interface for training, validation, and prediction.

### Initialization Parameters

```mermaid
graph LR
    AESTETIKModel["AESTETIKModel"]
    
    subgraph "Parameter Groups"
        grid["grid_params<br/>obsm_transcriptomics_dim"]
        arch["model_architecture_params<br/>kernel_size, latent_dim<br/>n_ensemble_encoder, n_ensemble_decoder<br/>c_hid, p"]
        train["training_params<br/>rec_alpha, triplet_alpha"]
        opt["optimizer_params<br/>lr, weight_decay"]
        dm["datamodule<br/>AESTETIKDataModule"]
    end
    
    grid --> AESTETIKModel
    arch --> AESTETIKModel
    train --> AESTETIKModel
    opt --> AESTETIKModel
    dm --> AESTETIKModel
```

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/modules/aestetik_module.py:15-55]()

### Key Methods

| Method | Parameters | Returns | Purpose |
|--------|-----------|---------|---------|
| `setup()` | `stage` | `None` | Initialize loss functions and weights from datamodule |
| `configure_model()` | - | `None` | Build the `AE` model with grid parameters |
| `training_step()` | `batch`, `batch_idx` | `Tensor` | Compute forward pass and loss for training |
| `validation_step()` | `batch`, `batch_idx` | `Tensor` | Compute validation loss with gradient tracking disabled |
| `predict_step()` | `batch`, `batch_idx`, `dataloader_idx` | `Tensor` | Generate latent embeddings with Monte Carlo dropout |
| `configure_optimizers()` | - | `Optimizer` | Configure Adam optimizer with AMSGrad |

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/modules/aestetik_module.py:68-168]()

### Model Configuration

The model is lazily initialized in `configure_model()` to allow dynamic grid parameter determination:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant L as Lightning Trainer
    participant M as AESTETIKModel
    participant D as DataModule
    participant A as AE
    
    L->>M: configure_model()
    M->>M: Check model_built flag
    M->>D: Access adata.obsm["X_st_grid"]
    D-->>M: Grid shape information
    M->>M: Set morphology_dim
    M->>M: Set num_input_channels
    M->>A: Initialize AE(**params)
    A-->>M: model instance
    M->>M: Set model_built = True
```

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/modules/aestetik_module.py:80-91]()

---

## AE Autoencoder Architecture

The `AE` class implements the core convolutional autoencoder with ensemble components. Both encoder and decoder use multiple independent networks whose outputs are combined via median aggregation.

### Architecture Overview

```mermaid
graph TB
    Input["Input Grid<br/>N × C × H × W"]
    
    subgraph "Encoder Ensemble"
        E1["Encode 1"]
        E2["Encode 2"]
        EN["Encode N"]
        MedianEnc["Median Aggregation"]
    end
    
    Latent["Latent Space<br/>N × latent_dim"]
    
    subgraph "Decoder Ensemble"
        D1["Decode 1"]
        D2["Decode 2"]
        DM["Decode M"]
        MedianDec["Median Aggregation"]
    end
    
    Output["Reconstructed Grid<br/>N × C × H × W"]
    
    Input --> E1
    Input --> E2
    Input --> EN
    E1 --> MedianEnc
    E2 --> MedianEnc
    EN --> MedianEnc
    MedianEnc --> Latent
    Latent --> D1
    Latent --> D2
    Latent --> DM
    D1 --> MedianDec
    D2 --> MedianDec
    DM --> MedianDec
    MedianDec --> Output
```

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/models/model.py:51-98]()

### Constructor Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `num_input_channels` | `int` | Total number of channels (transcriptomics + morphology) |
| `morphology_dim` | `int` | Spatial dimension of input grid (height/width) |
| `c_hid` | `int` | Number of hidden channels in convolutional layers |
| `latent_dim` | `int` | Dimensionality of latent representation |
| `kernel_size` | `int` | Size of convolutional kernels |
| `p` | `float` | Dropout probability |
| `n_ensemble_encoder` | `int` | Number of encoder networks (default: 2) |
| `n_ensemble_decoder` | `int` | Number of decoder networks (default: 1) |

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/models/model.py:52-62]()

### Forward Pass Methods

The `AE` class provides three methods for inference:

```mermaid
graph LR
    AE["AE Model"]
    
    encoder["encoder(x)<br/>Returns: latent_space"]
    decoder["decoder(latent)<br/>Returns: reconstruction"]
    forward["forward(x)<br/>Returns: latent, reconstruction"]
    
    AE --> encoder
    AE --> decoder
    AE --> forward
    
    forward -.-> encoder
    forward -.-> decoder
```

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/models/model.py:82-97]()

---

## Encoder Architecture (Encode Class)

The `Encode` class implements a single convolutional encoder network. Multiple instances are used in the ensemble.

### Layer Structure

```mermaid
graph TD
    Input["Input<br/>N × num_input_channels × H × W"]
    
    Conv["Conv2d<br/>kernel_size, stride=1"]
    BN1["BatchNorm2d"]
    Drop1["Dropout2d(p)"]
    ReLU1["ReLU"]
    Pool["MaxPool2d<br/>kernel_size, stride=3"]
    Flat["Flatten"]
    Linear["Linear<br/>conv_out_2² × c_hid → latent_dim"]
    
    Output["Output<br/>N × 1 × latent_dim"]
    
    Input --> Conv
    Conv --> BN1
    BN1 --> Drop1
    Drop1 --> ReLU1
    ReLU1 --> Pool
    Pool --> Flat
    Flat --> Linear
    Linear --> Output
```

**Spatial Dimension Calculations:**

The spatial dimensions are computed during `AE.__init__()`:
- `conv_out_1 = (morphology_dim - kernel_size) + 1`
- `conv_out_2 = floor((conv_out_1 - kernel_size) / 3 + 1)`

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/models/model.py:8-26](), [src/aestetik/models/model.py:65-66]()

### Implementation Details

The encoder is implemented as a `nn.Sequential` module containing all layers. The `forward()` method adds a singleton dimension to output shape `(batch_size, 1, latent_dim)` for ensemble concatenation.

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/models/model.py:13-26]()

---

## Decoder Architecture (Decode Class)

The `Decode` class implements a single convolutional decoder network that reconstructs the input from latent space.

### Layer Structure

```mermaid
graph TD
    Input["Input<br/>N × latent_dim"]
    
    Linear["Linear<br/>latent_dim → conv_out_2² × c_hid"]
    Unflatten["Unflatten<br/>→ (c_hid, conv_out_2, conv_out_2)"]
    ReLU["ReLU"]
    Upsample["UpsamplingNearest2d<br/>→ (conv_out_1, conv_out_1)"]
    Drop["Dropout2d(p)"]
    ConvT["ConvTranspose2d<br/>kernel_size, stride=1"]
    BN["BatchNorm2d"]
    Sigmoid["Sigmoid"]
    
    Output["Output<br/>N × 1 × num_input_channels × H × W"]
    
    Input --> Linear
    Linear --> Unflatten
    Unflatten --> ReLU
    ReLU --> Upsample
    Upsample --> Drop
    Drop --> ConvT
    ConvT --> BN
    BN --> Sigmoid
    Sigmoid --> Output
```

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/models/model.py:29-48]()

### Reconstruction Process

The decoder reverses the encoder operations:
1. Linear expansion from latent space
2. Reshape to spatial feature map
3. Upsampling to intermediate size
4. Transposed convolution to original spatial dimensions
5. Sigmoid activation for bounded output values

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/models/model.py:34-43]()

---

## Ensemble Mechanism

### Median Aggregation Strategy

Both encoder and decoder ensembles use median aggregation for robust predictions:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Input
    participant E1 as Encoder 1
    participant E2 as Encoder 2
    participant EN as Encoder N
    participant Agg as Aggregation
    
    Input->>E1: forward(x)
    Input->>E2: forward(x)
    Input->>EN: forward(x)
    E1-->>Agg: output₁
    E2-->>Agg: output₂
    EN-->>Agg: outputₙ
    Agg->>Agg: torch.cat(outputs, dim=1)
    Agg->>Agg: torch.median(outputs, dim=1)
    Agg-->>Input: median_output
```

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/models/model.py:82-92]()

### Code Implementation

#### Encoder Ensemble

```
x_encode = [unit(x) for unit in self.encoder_ensemble]
x_encode = torch.cat(x_encode, 1)
x_encode_median, _ = torch.median(x_encode, 1)
```

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/models/model.py:82-86]()

#### Decoder Ensemble

```
x_decode = [unit(x) for unit in self.decoder_ensemble]
x_decode = torch.cat(x_decode, 1)
x_decode_median, _ = torch.median(x_decode, 1)
```

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/models/model.py:88-92]()

### Rationale

Median aggregation provides robustness to outlier predictions from individual ensemble members, unlike mean aggregation which can be skewed by extreme values.

---

## Loss Computation

The loss function combines reconstruction and triplet losses for both modalities.

### Loss Components

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Reconstruction Losses"
        RecT["rec_loss_transcriptomics<br/>L1Loss"]
        RecM["rec_loss_morphology<br/>L1Loss"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Triplet Losses"
        TripT["triplet_loss_transcriptomics<br/>TripletMarginLoss"]
        TripM["triplet_loss_morphology<br/>TripletMarginLoss"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Weighting"
        Weights["transcriptomics_weight<br/>morphology_weight"]
        Alphas["rec_alpha<br/>triplet_alpha"]
    end
    
    RecT --> Total["Total Loss"]
    RecM --> Total
    TripT --> Total
    TripM --> Total
    Weights --> Total
    Alphas --> Total
```

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/metrics/loss_function.py:39-89]()

### Loss Formula

The total loss is computed as:

```
total_loss = transcriptomics_weight × (rec_alpha × rec_loss_transcriptomics + 
                                        triplet_alpha × triplet_loss_transcriptomics) +
             morphology_weight × (rec_alpha × rec_loss_morphology + 
                                  triplet_alpha × triplet_loss_morphology)
```

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/metrics/loss_function.py:86-87]()

### Loss Function Interface

| Function | Parameters | Returns | Purpose |
|----------|-----------|---------|---------|
| `compute_loss()` | `model`, `anchor`, `anchor_encode`, `anchor_decode`, positive/negative lists, weights, alphas | `Tuple[Tensor, ...]` | Compute all loss components |
| `compute_reconstruction_loss()` | `anchor`, `anchor_decode`, `loss` | `Tensor` | L1 loss between input and reconstruction |
| `compute_average_triplet_loss()` | `model`, `anchor_encode`, `pos_list`, `neg_list`, `loss`, `device` | `Tensor` | Average triplet loss over samples |

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/metrics/loss_function.py:4-89]()

### Triplet Loss Computation

Triplet loss uses anchor, positive, and negative samples from the same/different clusters:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Anchor
    participant P as Positive Samples
    participant N as Negative Samples
    participant E as Encoder
    participant L as TripletMarginLoss
    
    A->>E: Encode anchor
    E-->>A: anchor_encode
    P->>E: Encode positives (batch)
    E-->>P: pos_encodes
    N->>E: Encode negatives (batch)
    E-->>N: neg_encodes
    A->>L: (anchor, pos, neg)
    P->>L: Multiple samples
    N->>L: Multiple samples
    L-->>A: Average loss
```

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/metrics/loss_function.py:4-29]()

---

## Training Workflow

### Training Step Implementation

The `training_step()` method in `AESTETIKModel` orchestrates the forward pass and loss computation:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant T as Trainer
    participant M as AESTETIKModel
    participant AE as AE Model
    participant L as compute_loss
    
    T->>M: training_step(batch, batch_idx)
    M->>M: Unpack batch
    Note over M: anchor, pos_trans_list, neg_trans_list<br/>pos_morph_list, neg_morph_list
    M->>AE: forward(anchor)
    AE-->>M: anchor_encode, anchor_decode
    M->>L: compute_loss(...)
    L-->>M: total_loss, component_losses
    M->>M: Log metrics (L, RC, RI, TC, TI)
    M-->>T: total_loss
```

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/modules/aestetik_module.py:93-117]()

### Logged Metrics

| Metric Key | Description |
|------------|-------------|
| `L` | Total loss |
| `RC` | Reconstruction loss (transcriptomics) |
| `RI` | Reconstruction loss (morphology/image) |
| `TC` | Triplet loss (transcriptomics) |
| `TI` | Triplet loss (morphology/image) |

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/modules/aestetik_module.py:112-116]()

---

## Prediction Workflow

### Monte Carlo Dropout Prediction

The `predict_step()` method uses Monte Carlo dropout for uncertainty estimation:

```mermaid
graph TD
    Input["Input Batch"]
    
    ModelTrain["Set model.train()<br/>Keep dropout active"]
    
    Loop["Repeat num_repeats times"]
    
    Forward["encoder(batch)"]
    Store["Store latent output"]
    
    Stack["Stack outputs<br/>dim=0"]
    Mean["torch.mean(dim=0)"]
    
    Output["Averaged Latent Space"]
    
    Input --> ModelTrain
    ModelTrain --> Loop
    Loop --> Forward
    Forward --> Store
    Store --> Loop
    Loop --> Stack
    Stack --> Mean
    Mean --> Output
```

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/modules/aestetik_module.py:142-161]()

### Implementation Details

The prediction process:
1. Sets model to training mode to keep dropout layers active
2. Performs multiple forward passes (`num_repeats` times)
3. Averages the latent representations across repeats
4. Returns mean latent space for each batch

This approach provides more robust embeddings by sampling from the dropout distribution.

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/modules/aestetik_module.py:151-161]()

---

## Validation Workflow

The validation step is similar to training but with gradients disabled:

```mermaid
graph LR
    Val["validation_step()"]
    Train["Set model.train()"]
    NoGrad["with torch.no_grad()"]
    Forward["Forward pass"]
    Loss["Compute loss"]
    Log["Log val_loss"]
    
    Val --> Train
    Train --> NoGrad
    NoGrad --> Forward
    Forward --> Loss
    Loss --> Log
```

**Key differences from training:**
- Wrapped in `torch.no_grad()` context
- Only logs `val_loss` (total loss)
- Model still in training mode to maintain dropout behavior

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/modules/aestetik_module.py:119-140]()

---

## Optimizer Configuration

The `configure_optimizers()` method sets up the Adam optimizer:

```python
optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(
    self.model.parameters(),
    amsgrad=True,
    lr=optimizer_params["lr"],
    weight_decay=optimizer_params["weight_decay"]
)
```

**Configuration:**
- Algorithm: Adam with AMSGrad variant
- Adaptive learning rates for all model parameters
- L2 regularization via `weight_decay`

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/modules/aestetik_module.py:163-168]()

---

## Parameter Validation

Both `AESTETIKModel` and `AE` validate their parameters during initialization to ensure all required fields are present.

### Required Parameters by Group

| Parameter Group | Required Keys |
|----------------|---------------|
| `grid_params` | `obsm_transcriptomics_dim` |
| `model_architecture_params` | `kernel_size`, `latent_dim`, `n_ensemble_encoder`, `n_ensemble_decoder`, `c_hid`, `p` |
| `training_params` | `rec_alpha`, `triplet_alpha` |
| `optimizer_params` | `lr`, `weight_decay` |

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/modules/aestetik_module.py:171-185]()

---

## Callbacks

AESTETIK provides a custom callback for tracking training loss history:

### LossHistoryCallback

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class Callback {
        <<PyTorch Lightning>>
    }
    
    class LossHistoryCallback {
        +losses: List
        +on_train_batch_end()
    }
    
    Callback <|-- LossHistoryCallback
```

**Purpose:** Records loss values at the end of each training batch for visualization and analysis.

**Usage:** Automatically invoked by Lightning Trainer during training.

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/callbacks/callbacks.py:1-18]()

---

## Summary

The AESTETIK model architecture consists of:

1. **Lightning Wrapper (`AESTETIKModel`)**: Handles training orchestration, validation, and prediction workflows
2. **Core Autoencoder (`AE`)**: Convolutional encoder-decoder with ensemble members
3. **Encoder (`Encode`)**: Conv2d → BatchNorm → Dropout → MaxPool → Linear layers
4. **Decoder (`Decode`)**: Linear → Unflatten → Upsample → ConvTranspose2d → Sigmoid layers
5. **Ensemble Mechanism**: Median aggregation across multiple encoders/decoders
6. **Multi-Component Loss**: Reconstruction (L1) + Triplet losses for both modalities
7. **Monte Carlo Dropout**: Multiple forward passes during prediction for robust embeddings

This architecture enables robust learning of multi-modal spatial transcriptomics embeddings while maintaining spatial neighborhood information through grid-based inputs.

---

# Utility Functions

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/aestetik/utils/utils_clustering.py](src/aestetik/utils/utils_clustering.py)
- [src/aestetik/utils/utils_visualization.py](src/aestetik/utils/utils_visualization.py)

</details>



This page documents the utility functions in AESTETIK that support clustering, visualization, and analysis workflows. These utilities are primarily used after model training and prediction to analyze and visualize results.

For information about the main AESTETIK orchestrator class, see [AESTETIK Class](#5.1). For data preprocessing utilities used during training, see [Data Pipeline Components](#5.2). For visualization workflows and examples, see [Visualization](#4.5).

---

## Overview

AESTETIK provides two main utility modules:

| Module | Purpose | Primary Use Case |
|--------|---------|------------------|
| `utils_visualization.py` | Visualizing model outputs, clusters, and centroids | Post-prediction analysis and result interpretation |
| `utils_clustering.py` | Clustering embeddings and optimizing cluster parameters | Converting embeddings into discrete spatial domains |

These utilities operate on `AnnData` objects and integrate with the scanpy/squidpy ecosystem, following standard conventions for storing results in `.obs` and `.obsm` attributes.

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/utils/utils_visualization.py:1-256](), [src/aestetik/utils/utils_clustering.py:1-276]()

---

## Utility Integration Architecture

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "User Workflow"
        User["User Code"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Main API"
        AESTETIK["AESTETIK.predict()<br/>(with cluster=True)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Visualization Module"
        visualize["visualize()"]
        plot_loss["_plot_loss_values()"]
        plot_clusters["_plot_spatial_scatter_ari()"]
        plot_centroids["_plot_spatial_centroids_and_distance()"]
        compute_centroid["_compute_centroid()"]
        compute_morph["_compute_centroid_morphology()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Clustering Module"
        clustering["clustering()"]
        find_optimal["find_optimal_n_clusters()"]
        search_res["search_res()"]
        refine["_refine_cluster()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Data Storage"
        AnnData["AnnData Object<br/>adata.obs<br/>adata.obsm"]
    end
    
    User -->|"fit() + predict()"| AESTETIK
    AESTETIK -->|"internally calls"| clustering
    User -->|"visualize results"| visualize
    User -->|"optimize params"| find_optimal
    User -->|"manual clustering"| clustering
    
    visualize --> plot_loss
    visualize --> plot_clusters
    visualize --> plot_centroids
    visualize --> compute_centroid
    visualize --> compute_morph
    
    clustering --> search_res
    clustering --> refine
    
    clustering -->|"writes clusters to"| AnnData
    compute_centroid -->|"reads embeddings from"| AnnData
    compute_centroid -->|"writes centroids to"| AnnData
    plot_clusters -->|"reads clusters from"| AnnData
    
    style visualize fill:#e1f5ff,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style clustering fill:#fff4e1,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style AnnData fill:#e1ffe1,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
```

**Sources:** [src/aestetik/utils/utils_visualization.py:30-103](), [src/aestetik/utils/utils_clustering.py:140-211]()
